people.name: Nebuchadnezzar II
people.bio: King of Babylon who ruled from 605 to 562 BC. He rebuilt the city and its gates, and his builders faced the Ishtar Gate and the Processional Way with glazed brick.

milestones.event: Ordered the Ishtar Gate and the Processional Way in Babylon, faced with glazed moulded bricks.
German excavators uncovered the Ishtar Gate, whose glazed bricks reached Berlin for the rebuilt gate.

people.name: Exekias
people.bio: Athenian potter and painter who worked from about 545 to 530 BC. He signed his vases and gave black-figure painting its finest line, with a closer, quieter drama than earlier painters.

milestones.event: Painted and signed the amphora of Achilles and Ajax at a game of dice, now in the Vatican Museums.

people.name: Euphronios
people.bio: Athenian painter and potter of about 535 to 470 BC. He was one of the pioneers of red-figure painting and drew the body in foreshortened and natural poses.

milestones.event: Painted the calyx krater of the death of Sarpedon, one of the first masterworks of red-figure.

people.name: Qin Shi Huang
people.bio: First emperor of China. He ordered the tomb at Mount Li near Lintong, where state workshops made the army of life-size clay soldiers.

milestones.event: Unified China as its first emperor, and started the tomb complex at Lintong with its clay army.
Farmers who dug a well found the clay army that he ordered for his tomb.

people.name: Marcus Perennius Tigranus
people.bio: Potter of Arretium who ran a large workshop for red-gloss tableware. His stamp is on many moulded bowls and plates.

milestones.event: His workshop at Arezzo stamped his name on red-gloss bowls with moulded relief (an approximate year).

people.name: Abu Ibrahim Ahmad ibn Muhammad
people.bio: Aghlabid emir of Ifriqiya from 856 to 863. He enlarged the Great Mosque of Kairouan and had its mihrab faced with lustre tiles, the oldest lustre tiles that are still in place.

milestones.event: Had the mihrab of the Great Mosque of Kairouan faced with lustre tiles from Iraq.

people.name: Abbot Suger
people.bio: Abbot of Saint-Denis. He raised the money and ordered the rebuilding of the abbey church that began Gothic architecture.

milestones.event: Ordered the new choir of the abbey church.
Dedicated the rebuilt choir of the Basilica of Saint-Denis in the presence of the king.
Died with the rebuilding unfinished.

people.name: Celaleddin Karatay
people.bio: Seljuk emir and statesman of the 13th century. He paid for the Karatay Madrasa in Konya, whose dome and entrance hall are covered with cut-tile mosaic in turquoise, blue and black.

milestones.event: Founded the Karatay Madrasa in Konya, with a tile-mosaic dome.

people.name: Abu Inan Faris
people.bio: Marinid sultan of Morocco from 1348. He ordered the Bou Inania Madrasa in Fez, where zellige covers the walls of the court and the lower part of the prayer hall.

milestones.event: Ordered the Bou Inania Madrasa in Fez, built in the 1350s, with zellige on its walls.

people.name: Charles V of France
people.bio: King of France from 1364. As Duke of Normandy he employed the cook Taillevent from 1359.

emblem.credit: Wikimedia Commons contributors; see the file page

milestones.event: Made Taillevent his chief cook.

people.name: Guillaume Tirel
people.bio: French cook known as Taillevent. He rose from a kitchen boy to the chief cook of the royal kitchens, and the book Le Viandier carries his name.

milestones.event: Became chief cook of the kitchen of King Charles V.
Became squire of the kitchen of King Charles VI.

people.name: Yongle Emperor
people.bio: Third emperor of the Ming dynasty. He moved the capital to Beijing and ordered the Forbidden City, whose halls carry the yellow glazed roof of the imperial kilns.

milestones.event: Ordered the work on the Forbidden City in Beijing, which began this year.
Saw the palace complete; its main halls have roofs of imperial yellow glazed tile.

people.name: Zheng He
people.bio: Ming admiral who led seven treasure-fleet voyages across the Indian Ocean. The ships carried Chinese ceramics, with Longquan celadon among them, to the ports of South-East Asia, India and East Africa.

milestones.event: Began the first of seven voyages that took Chinese ceramics to the Indian Ocean ports.

people.name: Filippo Brunelleschi
people.bio: Florentine architect. He built the dome of Florence Cathedral from 1420 to 1436 for the wool guild.

milestones.event: Began the dome of Florence Cathedral.
Took sole charge of the dome of Florence Cathedral.
Completed the dome of Florence Cathedral.

people.name: Philip the Good
people.bio: Duke of Burgundy from 1419 to 1467. His court bought Valencian lustre tiles and dishes for its palaces, and so it helped to spread Hispano-Moresque ware in northern Europe.

people.name: Xuande Emperor
people.bio: Ming emperor from 1425 to 1435. Under his rule the imperial kilns at Jingdezhen made blue-and-white porcelain of the highest quality and began to mark it with the reign title.

milestones.event: Became emperor; the imperial kilns at Jingdezhen reached a high point of blue-and-white porcelain in his reign.

people.name: Johannes Gutenberg
people.bio: German goldsmith and inventor who built the movable-type press in Mainz and printed his Bible in a textura blackletter type.

milestones.event: Had his press in operation in Mainz.
Completed the printing of the Gutenberg Bible in textura type.

people.name: Luca della Robbia
people.bio: Florentine sculptor. He made marble work first, then found a way to cover terracotta sculpture with a white tin glaze. His family workshop made glazed reliefs for churches for three generations.

milestones.event: Began the glazed terracotta lunette of the Resurrection for Florence Cathedral.

people.name: Michael Wolgemut
people.bio: Nuremberg painter whose workshop cut the woodcuts for large printed books.

milestones.event: Took the young Dürer as an apprentice.
His workshop supplied the woodcuts for the Nuremberg Chronicle.

people.name: Ashikaga Yoshimasa
people.bio: Eighth shogun of the Ashikaga family and a great collector of Chinese art. His store of Chinese tea ware, with Jian tenmoku bowls, set the standard for tea in Japan.

milestones.event: Began the Silver Pavilion at Higashiyama, where he kept his Chinese tea bowls and tea ware.

people.name: Pope Julius II
people.bio: Pope who commissioned Michelangelo to paint the Sistine ceiling and Raphael to decorate the papal rooms.

milestones.event: Signed the contract for the Sistine Chapel ceiling.

people.name: Sandro Botticelli
people.bio: Italian painter of the early Renaissance in Florence.

milestones.event: Painted The Birth of Venus.

people.name: Leonardo da Vinci
people.bio: Italian painter, engineer and scientist of the High Renaissance.

milestones.event: Completed The Last Supper in Milan.
Started the Mona Lisa.

people.name: Ludovico Sforza
people.bio: Ruler of Milan from 1479 to 1499. Leonardo da Vinci worked in his service from 1482.

milestones.event: Leonardo began to work in Milan in his service.

people.name: Niculoso Pisano
people.bio: Italian potter who settled in Seville in 1498. He brought the Italian painted maiolica tile to Spain and made the first tile pictures in the style that became the azulejo.

milestones.event: Settled in Seville and opened a tile workshop in Triana.
Made the tile Visitation for the chapel of the Alcázar of Seville.

people.name: Albrecht Dürer
people.bio: German painter and printmaker who made the woodcut and the engraving into major art forms.

milestones.event: Published the Apocalypse, a set of sixteen woodcuts.
Engraved Melencolia I and St Jerome in His Study.

people.name: Hans Burgkmair
people.bio: German painter and woodcut designer in Augsburg. He cut some of the first chiaroscuro woodcuts, and he worked for Emperor Maximilian I.

milestones.event: Cut a three-block chiaroscuro woodcut in Augsburg.

people.name: Michelangelo
people.bio: Italian sculptor, painter and architect. He painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling for Pope Julius II.

milestones.event: Signed the contract for the Sistine Chapel ceiling for 3,000 ducats.

people.name: Ugo da Carpi
people.bio: Italian printmaker who brought the chiaroscuro woodcut to Italy. He cut tone-block prints after Raphael and Parmigianino, with no line block.

milestones.event: Asked the Venetian authorities for a patent on his chiaroscuro woodcuts.

people.name: Raphael
people.bio: Italian painter of balanced High Renaissance compositions.

milestones.event: Completed The School of Athens in the Vatican.

people.name: Claude Garamond
people.bio: French punch-cutter in Paris whose roman types became the model for the old-style book face.

milestones.event: Became known for the Greek types made for Robert Estienne.

people.name: Francis I of France
people.bio: King of France. He took Leonardo da Vinci into his service in 1516 and gave him the manor Clos Lucé.

emblem.credit: Wikimedia Commons contributors; see the file page

milestones.event: Took Leonardo into his service.

people.name: Nicola da Urbino
people.bio: Maiolica painter of Urbino and the best-known master of the istoriato style. His plates show whole scenes from Ovid and the Bible, copied from prints by engravers of his day.

milestones.event: Painted a large dinner service for Isabella d'Este, a work that is dated to about this year.

people.name: Pontormo
people.bio: Florentine painter whose twisting figures and acid colour set the manner of early Mannerism.

milestones.event: Completed The Deposition from the Cross in the Capponi Chapel in Florence.

people.name: Suleiman the Magnificent
people.bio: Ottoman sultan from 1520 to 1566. His building programme, with the tile repair of the Dome of the Rock from about 1545, gave the Iznik potteries their largest orders.

emblem.credit: Tughra_of_Suleiman_I_the_Magnificent.JPG: Unknown court calligrapher. derivative work: Alberto Fernandez Fernandez (talk)

milestones.event: Ordered new tile panels for the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem from the Iznik workshops.

people.name: Chōjirō
people.bio: Kyoto tile maker who became the first potter of Raku ware. He built black and red tea bowls by hand for the tea master Sen no Rikyū.

milestones.event: Made the first hand-built black and red tea bowls for the tea master Sen no Rikyū (about this year).

people.name: Hieronymus Cock
people.bio: Antwerp publisher who split print work into design, engraving and sale.

milestones.event: Founded the print house Aux Quatre Vents in Antwerp.
Published his own last series, twelve landscape etchings.

people.name: Matthieu Cointerel
people.bio: French cardinal who died in 1585. His endowment paid for the Contarelli Chapel in Rome.

milestones.event: Cointerel bought the rights to a chapel in San Luigi dei Francesi in Rome.
Caravaggio signed the contract for the paintings of his chapel.

people.name: Cipriano Piccolpasso
people.bio: Italian writer and potter. His manuscript of about 1557, The Three Books of the Potter's Art, is the first full record of how maiolica makers worked, with kilns, tools and drug-jar shapes.

milestones.event: Wrote the manuscript on the potter's art, with drawings of drug jars and kilns.

people.name: Mimar Sinan
people.bio: Chief architect of the Ottoman court for about 50 years. He used Iznik tiles on the walls of his mosques and tombs, most clearly in the Rüstem Pasha Mosque in Istanbul.

milestones.event: Completed the Rüstem Pasha Mosque in Istanbul, with Iznik tiles on the walls and the porch.
Completed the mausoleum of Süleyman the Magnificent, with Iznik tiles in the new emerald green.

people.name: Jan Emens
people.bio: Stoneware potter of Raeren, near Aachen. His jugs carry his mark and dates from 1568 to 1594. He made the relief friezes of the Raeren Bartmann and tankard type.

milestones.event: Made the first of his dated salt-glazed jugs in Raeren.
Made the last of his dated jugs, with a relief frieze.

people.name: Bartolomeo Scappi
people.bio: Italian cook of cardinals and popes. His Opera of 1570 holds about 1,000 recipes and shows the tools and the stations of a Renaissance kitchen.

milestones.event: Published the Opera dell'arte del cucinare in Venice.
Died in Rome.

people.name: Furuta Oribe
people.bio: Warrior and tea master who ordered bold, bent tea ware from the Mino kilns. The green Oribe glaze bears his name.

milestones.event: Became a leading tea master of Japan after the death of Sen no Rikyū.

people.name: Hendrick Goltzius
people.bio: Dutch engraver whose swelling lines set a standard for the engraved print.

milestones.event: Moved to Haarlem and engraved a Lucretia series for Philip Galle.
Travelled to Italy to study the art of Rome.

people.name: Jacob van Heemskerck
people.bio: Dutch naval officer. In 1603 he took the Portuguese ship Santa Catarina, and its cargo of Chinese porcelain went on sale in Amsterdam.

milestones.event: Captured the Portuguese ship Santa Catarina with a cargo of Chinese blue-and-white porcelain.

people.name: Caravaggio
people.bio: Italian painter whose strong light and dark changed European painting.

milestones.event: Completed The Calling of Saint Matthew in Rome.
Died on the way back to Rome.

people.name: Marie de' Medici
people.bio: Queen of France and widow of Henry IV. She commissioned the Luxembourg Palace cycle from Rubens.

milestones.event: Gave Rubens the commission for the Luxembourg Palace cycle.

people.name: Peter Paul Rubens
people.bio: Flemish painter of dynamic Baroque scenes.

milestones.event: Painted The Elevation of the Cross.

people.name: Hu Zhengyan
people.bio: Chinese painter, printer and publisher in Nanjing. He ran the Ten Bamboo Studio, and made its colour albums and its embossed letter paper.

milestones.event: Published the Manual of Painting and Calligraphy of the Ten Bamboo Studio.
Published the Letter Paper, a set with embossed (gonghua) patterns.

people.name: Jacques Callot
people.bio: Printmaker from Lorraine who made etching a precise medium with a hard ground and the échoppe needle.

photo.credit: Ignazio Enrico Hugford, after Antoon van Dyck (1599–1641), painter of the original

milestones.event: Started work in Florence for the Medici court.
Returned to Nancy and etched there for the rest of his life.

people.name: Sakaida Kakiemon I
people.bio: Potter of Arita. By the tradition of his family he found a clear red enamel for porcelain in the 1640s, and the milk-white body and sparse red, blue and green painting of his workshop became the Kakiemon style.

milestones.event: Is said to have made the first red overglaze enamel at Arita, by the tradition of the Kakiemon family.

people.name: Francesco Borromini
people.bio: Italian architect in Rome who bent walls and domes into curves and made the Baroque church a work of geometry.

milestones.event: Received the commission for San Carlo alle Quattro Fontane in Rome.

people.name: Rembrandt
people.bio: Dutch painter of light, shadow and portraits.

milestones.event: Made his first etchings.
Painted The Night Watch.
Cut The Three Crosses in drypoint, with a thick burr in the dark areas.

people.name: Ludwig von Siegen
people.bio: German soldier and amateur artist who made the first known mezzotint.

milestones.event: Finished the first known mezzotint, a portrait of Amalia Elisabeth, Landgravine of Hesse-Kassel.

people.name: Nonomura Ninsei
people.bio: Kyoto potter who painted tea jars in enamel and gold. He worked at the Omuro kiln near the temple of Ninna-ji and signed his work with a seal.

milestones.event: Opened a kiln at Omuro, below the temple of Ninna-ji in Kyoto (about this year).

people.name: Hishikawa Moronobu
people.bio: Japanese artist who made ukiyo-e into a form of single-sheet prints.

milestones.event: Signed his first illustrated books in Edo.

people.name: François Pierre de La Varenne
people.bio: French cook of the Marquis d'Uxelles. His book Le Cuisinier françois moved French cooking from heavy spice to stocks, roux and herbs.

source.title: Wikipedia: François Pierre de La Varenne

milestones.event: Published Le Cuisinier françois.
Published Le Pastissier françois.

people.name: Louis XIV
people.bio: King of France. He built Versailles and bought the Gobelins works through Colbert in 1662.

emblem.credit: Wikimedia Commons contributors; see the file page

milestones.event: Bought the Gobelins works through Colbert.
Made Hardouin-Mansart his first architect at Versailles.

people.name: Thomas Toft
people.bio: Staffordshire potter of the late 17th century. His large slip-trailed dishes, with royal arms, mermaids and pelicans, and his name in the rim, are the best known English slipware.

milestones.event: Made a dated slip-trailed dish in Staffordshire; his dishes carry dates up to the 1680s.

people.name: Jules Hardouin-Mansart
people.bio: First architect of Louis XIV from 1678. He built the Hall of Mirrors and the ministers' wings at Versailles.

milestones.event: Became first architect at Versailles.

people.name: Adriaen Kocks
people.bio: Delft potter who owned the pottery De Grieksche A from 1687. His workshop made the large flower pyramids and tiles for Queen Mary II and King William III.

milestones.event: Became the owner of the pottery De Grieksche A in Delft.
Made flower pyramids and tiles for the dairy and the water gallery of Queen Mary II at Hampton Court.
Made tiles for the dairy of Queen Mary II at Hampton Court.

people.name: Tang Ying
people.bio: Official of the Qing court who worked at the imperial kilns at Jingdezhen from 1728 and directed them from 1736. He ran the enamel colours and the range of forms for the Yongzheng and Qianlong emperors.

milestones.event: Went to Jingdezhen to help to run the imperial kilns.
Became the director of the imperial kilns.

people.name: Antoine Watteau
people.bio: French painter whose scenes of courtly leisure in soft colour led to the Rococo style.

milestones.event: Became a full member of the French Academy with the Embarkation for Cythera.

people.name: George Bickham the Elder
people.bio: English writing master and engraver whose collection The Universal Penman made the English round hand script common.

milestones.event: Started to publish The Universal Penman in parts.
Issued the last part of The Universal Penman.

people.name: Johann Joachim Kändler
people.bio: German sculptor who was chief modeller at the Meissen manufactory from 1733. He made the Harlequins, the Monkey Band and many lovers and shepherds of Meissen.

milestones.event: Joined the Meissen manufactory as a modeller.
Became the chief modeller of Meissen.

people.name: John Baskerville
people.bio: English printer who cut his own type with sharper contrast and a near vertical stress, and printed fine books with it.

milestones.event: Printed an edition of Virgil in his own type.
Printed a folio Bible in his own type.

people.name: Carl Johan Cronstedt
people.bio: Swedish architect and court official. With Wrede he made a design for a new, fuel-saving tiled stove after a Council commission, and the design set the form of the Swedish kakelugn.

milestones.event: Presented a stove design to the Council, with Wrede, after the commission of January 1767.

people.name: Louis XV
people.bio: King of France. He bought the Sèvres porcelain manufactory in 1759.

emblem.credit: Wikimedia Commons contributors; see the file page

milestones.event: Bought the Sèvres manufactory.

people.name: Thomas Frye
people.bio: Irish painter who ran the Bow porcelain factory in London. He took a patent in 1748 for a porcelain with bone ash, the base of English bone china.

milestones.event: Took out a first patent with Edward Heylyn for a porcelain made with American clay.
Took out a patent for a porcelain that contains bone ash.

people.name: Jacques-Germain Soufflot
people.bio: French architect in the first circle of Neoclassicism who designed the Panthéon in Paris.

milestones.event: Was chosen to design the Panthéon in Paris.

people.name: Ralph Wood
people.bio: Potter of Burslem, Staffordshire, who made earthenware figures and Toby jugs with coloured lead glazes. His son and grandson kept the works.

people.name: Étienne Maurice Falconet
people.bio: French sculptor who ran the sculpture studio of the Sèvres manufactory from 1757. His models after Boucher were cast in biscuit porcelain.

milestones.event: Became the head of the sculpture studio at Sèvres.

people.name: John Boydell
people.bio: London engraver and publisher who built an export trade in English prints.

milestones.event: Started his own engraving and print business in London.
Started the Shakespeare Gallery and its folio of engravings.

people.name: Dai Lianzeng
people.bio: Chinese craftsman of Yangliuqing. A Wikipedia account says that he brought colour woodblock print and hand colour to the town and set up its first large workshops. His dates are not known.

milestones.event: Set up workshops in Dongfengtai, near Tianjin (a date around the 1750s; sources differ).

people.name: Madame de Pompadour
people.bio: Official mistress of Louis XV. She led French taste in dress, silk and porcelain, and she paid for the Rococo style.

milestones.event: Became the official mistress of Louis XV and took the title of marquise.
Her support helped to move the royal porcelain manufactory from Vincennes to Sèvres.
Died at Versailles.

people.name: Suzuki Harunobu
people.bio: Japanese designer of woodblock prints. He and his printers made the first full-colour prints on many blocks, the nishiki-e, and drew slim, quiet young women.

milestones.event: Made the first full-colour prints on many blocks, for a calendar exchange of Edo patrons.

people.name: Sir Nathaniel Curzon
people.bio: English landowner. He commissioned Kedleston Hall and put Robert Adam in charge of the new house.

milestones.event: Commissioned the new house at Kedleston.

people.name: Francesco Bartolozzi
people.bio: Italian engraver in London. He made stipple engraving a fashion, and he printed some plates in colour.

milestones.event: Moved from Venice to London.
Engraved the stipple portrait of Francis Willis.

people.name: Matthew Boulton
people.bio: English manufacturer in Birmingham. He ran the Soho Manufactory, where workers made buttons, buckles and small metal goods, among them cut steel ornaments, in large numbers.

milestones.event: Opened the Soho Manufactory at Birmingham, a factory for small metal goods.

people.name: Robert Adam
people.bio: Scottish architect who designed the room as one whole, from the ceiling plaster to the carpet, in a light neoclassical manner.

milestones.event: Returned to London from his Grand Tour of Italy and started his practice.
Published the first volume of The Works in Architecture of Robert and James Adam.
Published the first volume of The Works in Architecture, a source of classical models for makers of furniture, metalwork and ceramics.

people.name: Catherine the Great
people.bio: Empress of Russia. She ordered the 952-piece Frog Service from Wedgwood in 1773.

milestones.event: Ordered the Frog Service from Wedgwood.

people.name: Josiah Wedgwood
people.bio: English potter who built the Etruria works in Staffordshire. After thousands of trials he made jasperware, a stained stoneware with white classical reliefs, in 1775.

milestones.event: Bought an engine-turning lathe for pots; the same tool cut the banded pearlware that other Staffordshire firms later coloured with mocha.
Made a cream-coloured tea service for Queen Charlotte; the ware took the name Queen's ware.
Opened the Etruria works in Staffordshire.
Introduced jasperware after thousands of trials.
Made the first edition of the Portland Vase in blue jasper.

people.name: Josiah Spode
people.bio: English potter who founded the Spode works at Stoke in 1770. His works made blue-and-white ware printed from engraved copper plates.

milestones.event: Founded the Spode pottery at Stoke-upon-Trent.

people.name: Jean-Baptiste Le Prince
people.bio: French painter and printmaker. His claim to the invention of aquatint is the one that dates from 1768 to 1769.

milestones.event: Began the aquatint work in Paris that gave him the main claim to the invention.

people.name: Ann Lee
people.bio: English religious leader who founded the Shaker movement in America, whose way of life gave the Shaker style.

milestones.event: Sailed to America with a small group of followers.
Sailed to New York with 8 followers; the community that she led later made the plain Shaker furniture and boxes.

people.name: Giambattista Bodoni
people.bio: Italian printer who cut high-contrast serif typefaces with thin hairlines, the model of elegant luxury type.

milestones.event: Became the printer of the ducal press at the court of Parma.
Published an edition of the Manuale tipografico.
His widow published the Manuale tipografico, the full book of his typefaces.

people.name: Francisco Goya
people.bio: Spanish painter and printmaker. He used aquatint with etching and burnishing to make the deep night tones of his print series.

milestones.event: Published Los Caprichos, a set of 80 prints in etching and aquatint.

people.name: Abraham-Louis Breguet
people.bio: Swiss-born watchmaker in Paris. He made watches with a clear dial, a thin case and a steel hand, and he patented the tourbillon in 1801.

milestones.event: Opened his watch workshop in Paris.
Patented the tourbillon, a cage that turns the escapement to cancel the effect of gravity.

people.name: Rose Bertin
people.bio: French milliner and dressmaker. She supplied Queen Marie Antoinette and set the trimmed, ribboned gown of the late Rococo court.

milestones.event: Born at Abbeville, Picardy.
By this year she supplied Queen Marie Antoinette with gowns and hats, and the court called her the Minister of Fashion.

people.name: John Raphael Smith
people.bio: English mezzotint engraver who reproduced the portraits of Reynolds and others.

milestones.event: Moved to London to start a print business.
Issued his mezzotint of Mrs Carnac after Reynolds.

people.name: Thomas Bewick
people.bio: English engraver in Newcastle. He cut the end grain of hard wood with a burin, and he is the usual founder of wood engraving.

milestones.event: Published A General History of Quadrupeds, with his wood engravings.
Published the first volume of A History of British Birds.

people.name: Robert Thorne
people.bio: British type founder whose later typefaces were very heavy Didones, the first fat faces made for posters and display.

milestones.event: Bought the type foundry of Thomas Cottrell and issued his first specimen.
Moved his foundry to Fann Street in Aldersgate.

people.name: Talleyrand
people.bio: French statesman. Carême ran his pastry kitchen at the Hôtel de Galliffet from 1803 to 1814.

milestones.event: Hired Carême as head pastry cook.

people.name: Josiah Spode II
people.bio: English potter who led the Spode works after his father. He made a bone china body that gave the pottery a strong, white porcelain.

milestones.event: Brought a stable bone china body into regular use at the Spode works.

people.name: Marie Antoinette
people.bio: Queen of France from 1774 to 1792. The court of Versailles under her dressed in stays and wide gowns, and her dress set the rule for French court fashion.

emblem.credit: Wikimedia Commons contributors; see the file page

milestones.event: Became queen of France; the court of Versailles wore boned stays under every formal gown.

people.name: Katsushika Hokusai
people.bio: Japanese ukiyo-e artist of landscapes and The Great Wave.

milestones.event: Designed the surimono series Genroku Poems and Shells.
Began to publish the Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji, with Prussian blue ink.
Published The Great Wave off Kanagawa in Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji.

people.name: George IV
people.bio: British king from 1820. As Prince Regent he hired Carême as chef at Carlton House in 1816.

milestones.event: Hired Carême as chef at Carlton House.

people.name: Joséphine de Beauharnais
people.bio: Empress of the French from 1804. Her light muslin gowns and cashmere shawls set the fashion for the high-waisted dress.

emblem.credit: Wikimedia Commons contributors; see the file page

milestones.event: Married Napoleon Bonaparte.
Crowned Empress at Notre-Dame; the court kept the high waist and the long, light line.

people.name: Jacob Perkins
people.bio: American inventor who made hardened steel plates for engraving. He moved to London to print bank notes that forgers could not copy.

milestones.event: Sailed to England to win the contract for forgery-proof bank notes.

people.name: Vincent Figgins
people.bio: English type founder whose London foundry showed the first slab serif and early sans serif capitals.

milestones.event: Issued a specimen of the first slab serif type, called Antique.
Showed sans serif capitals in a specimen.

people.name: Chen Mansheng
people.bio: Qing official, calligrapher and seal carver. He designed teapots in simple shapes with the Yixing potter Yang Pengnian and cut poems on the walls, in the style of the Mansheng pot.

people.name: Caspar David Friedrich
people.bio: German landscape painter whose lonely figures before vast nature are central images of Romanticism.

milestones.event: Completed Cross in the Mountains, also called the Tetschen Altar.

people.name: Clarkson Crolius
people.bio: New York stoneware potter of a family of German potters. His Manhattan works made salt-glazed jugs and crocks with a cobalt motif, and he also served in the United States Congress.

milestones.event: Led the Crolius stoneware pottery in Manhattan, which made salt-glazed crocks and jugs with cobalt decoration.

people.name: Beau Brummell
people.bio: English man of fashion at the court of the Prince Regent. He set the dark, plain, well-cut coat and the clean linen of the modern man's suit.

milestones.event: Took a commission in the 10th Light Dragoons, the Prince of Wales's regiment.
Fled to France to escape his debts, and left London dress to its tailors.

people.name: Marie-Antoine Carême
people.bio: French pastry cook and chef who worked for Talleyrand, the Prince Regent and the Rothschilds. He set the grand sauces in a system and built sugar and pastry monuments.

milestones.event: Published Le Pâtissier royal parisien and Le Pâtissier pittoresque.
Published Le Cuisinier parisien.
Died in Paris; his L'Art de la cuisine française was left unfinished.

people.name: Ramchand Roy
people.bio: Bengali woodcut cutter of Calcutta. One source credits him with the woodblock pictures of the Annadamangal of 1816.

milestones.event: Cut the woodblock pictures for the Bengali book Annadamangal, printed in Calcutta (one source credits him).

people.name: Yashima Gakutei
people.bio: Japanese artist, poet and pupil of the Hokusai circle. He designed many surimono prints for poetry clubs in Edo.

people.name: Mirza Saleh Shirazi
people.bio: Iranian court translator and diplomat (c.1790–c.1845). He learnt printing in London and founded a lithographic printing firm in Tabriz, with a press from Russia.

milestones.event: Came back to Iran from London with a printing press, after work as a printer's apprentice. Later he founded a lithographic press in Tabriz.

people.name: Herbert Minton
people.bio: English potter in Stoke-on-Trent who led the family firm Minton. He made the encaustic floor tile a mass product and sold it to the Gothic Revival churches and to the Palace of Westminster.

milestones.event: Won a council medal at the Great Exhibition for the Minton tiles.

people.name: Roxey Ann Caplin
people.bio: English corsetmaker and author. She argued for corsets that fit the body, wrote on dress and health, and filed many patents for corsets and crinolines.

milestones.event: Worked as a corsetmaker at 58 Berners Street, London.
Won a medal for her corsets at the Great Exhibition.
Held 24 patents by this year.

people.name: Utagawa Hiroshige
people.bio: Japanese ukiyo-e artist of travel landscapes.

milestones.event: Published The Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō.
Published the print Driving Rain at Shono in the Fifty-Three Stations of the Tokaido.
Started One Hundred Famous Views of Edo.

people.name: Darius Wells
people.bio: American printer who cut wood type by machine and made it cheap enough for posters.

milestones.event: Published his first known wood-type catalogue in New York.

people.name: Hiram Powers
people.bio: American sculptor in Florence. His marble Greek Slave toured Britain from 1845, and Staffordshire potters made small parian copies of it.

milestones.event: Showed the marble Greek Slave in London.

people.name: Henry Cole
people.bio: English civil servant and design reformer who organised the Great Exhibition of 1851 and founded the museum that became the Victoria and Albert Museum.

milestones.event: Began to sell household goods by good artists, as Summerly's Art Manufactures.
Helped to organise the Great Exhibition, which showed the goods of the machine age to 6 million visitors.

people.name: Honoré Daumier
people.bio: French caricaturist who drew on lithographic stone with a crayon. His daily prints made lithography the press of the political joke.

milestones.event: Began to draw lithographs for the Paris magazine Le Charivari.

people.name: Owen Jones
nationality: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
people.bio: Welsh-born British architect and designer who set out the rules of rich Victorian ornament and colour.

milestones.event: Worked as a Superintendent of Works and decorated the Crystal Palace for the Great Exhibition.
Published The Grammar of Ornament.

people.name: George Jennings
people.bio: English sanitary engineer. His public lavatories at the Crystal Palace in 1851 showed the flush toilet to millions of visitors.

milestones.event: Fitted flush toilets for public use at the Great Exhibition in the Crystal Palace.

people.name: Aaron Lufkin Dennison
people.bio: American watchmaker who set up the first American factory for machine-made watches with interchangeable parts. His firm became the Waltham Watch Company.

milestones.event: Founded the Boston Watch Company with Howard and Davis; the firm later became the Waltham Watch Company.

people.name: Julia Margaret Cameron
nationality: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
people.bio: British photographer of soft-focus portraits in the 1860s.

milestones.event: Started to take photographs.

people.name: Alphonse Poitevin
people.bio: French chemist and inventor. He found that hardened gelatin takes ink in proportion to light, and so he made the collotype.

milestones.event: Patented the collotype process.

people.name: Christopher Latham Sholes
people.bio: American printer and inventor who made the first commercially successful typewriter, the machine that gave each letter the same width.

milestones.event: Received a patent for his typewriter with Carlos Glidden and Samuel Soule.

people.name: Gustave Courbet
people.bio: French painter who led the Realist movement and showed ordinary people at life size.

milestones.event: Showed his paintings in his own Pavilion of Realism in Paris.

people.name: Queen Victoria
people.bio: British queen from 1837. Her court and her household set the manner of dress, and her elastic-sided boots made the style respectable.

milestones.event: Opened the Great Exhibition in London, where bootmakers showed their boots to a mass public.
Mourned Prince Albert, who died in December, and wore black mourning jewellery for many years; jet became the fashion.

people.name: Henry Doulton
people.bio: English potter who led the Lambeth pottery of his father. He made salt-glazed stoneware drain pipes, sanitary ware and sinks for the new city sewers.

milestones.event: Began to make stoneware sanitary pipes at Lambeth.

people.name: Louis Vuitton
people.bio: French trunk-maker. He opened his shop in Paris in 1854 and sold a flat-topped trunk in grey coated canvas that stacked and shed rain.

milestones.event: Opened his trunk-maker's shop in Paris and sold the flat-topped trunk in coated canvas.
Opened a workshop at Asnières, near Paris.
Added a striped canvas, the first pattern on his trunks.

people.name: Charles Frederick Worth
people.bio: English couturier in Paris. He founded the first modern fashion house and dressed the Second Empire court in the cage crinoline and then the bustle.

milestones.event: Opened the House of Worth at 7 rue de la Paix, Paris, with Otto Bobergh.
Became the dressmaker of Empress Eugénie after Princess Pauline de Metternich presented him.

people.name: Charles Garnier
people.bio: French architect trained at the École des Beaux-Arts who built the Paris Opera as the showpiece of the style.

milestones.event: Began the construction of the Paris Opera, now the Palais Garnier.
Opened the Paris Opera to the public.

people.name: Gustave Moreau
people.bio: French painter of myth and dream whose rich, strange pictures were a source for Symbolism.

milestones.event: Completed Salome Dancing before Herod.

people.name: William Holman Hunt
people.bio: English painter and a founder of the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood. He kept to its rules of close observation and moral subjects for his whole life.

milestones.event: Co-founded the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood.
Showed The Light of the World at the Royal Academy.

people.name: Cromwell Fleetwood Varley
people.bio: English telegraph engineer. He patented several stoneware insulator designs in 1861, among them the Z type, for the first long telegraph lines.

milestones.event: Patented several stoneware telegraph insulator designs, among them the Z type.

people.name: Dante Gabriel Rossetti
people.bio: English painter and poet. He was a co-founder of the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood and later painted dreamy, symbolic women.

milestones.event: Co-founded the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood in London.
Printed poems in The Germ, the journal of the Brotherhood.

people.name: John Everett Millais
people.bio: English painter who was a founder of the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood. He painted scenes from the Bible and from poetry in hard, bright detail taken from nature.

milestones.event: Co-founded the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood at his parents' house in London.

people.name: Levi Strauss
people.bio: German-born merchant of San Francisco. He backed the patent of Jacob Davis and made the riveted waist overall in his own factory.

milestones.event: Moved to San Francisco and opened a dry goods house.
Made the riveted waist overall under the patent that he shared with Jacob Davis.

people.name: Alfred Waterhouse
people.bio: English architect of the Gothic Revival. He clad the Natural History Museum in London and many town halls, banks and colleges in buff, red and blue-grey terracotta.

milestones.event: Opened the Natural History Museum in London, with a facade of moulded terracotta blocks.

people.name: Camille Pissarro
people.bio: Danish-French painter, the only one who showed at all eight Impressionist exhibitions.

milestones.event: Showed at the first Impressionist exhibition.

people.name: Eadweard Muybridge
people.bio: English photographer who studied the motion of animals with rows of cameras. His plates were printed as collotypes.

milestones.event: Published Animal Locomotion, with 781 plates printed as collotypes.

people.name: Jacob Davis
people.bio: Tailor of Reno, Nevada. He set copper rivets at the stress points of work trousers and, with Levi Strauss, took a patent for the idea in 1873.

milestones.event: Took US patent 139,121 with Levi Strauss for work trousers with riveted pockets.

people.name: Philip Webb
nationality: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
people.bio: British architect called the father of Arts and Crafts architecture, who built plain houses of local materials.

milestones.event: Designed the Red House at Bexleyheath for William Morris.

people.name: Ivan Shishkin
people.bio: Russian landscape painter of forests and fields. He was a founder-member of the Peredvizhniki.

milestones.event: Joined the founders of the Society for Travelling Art Exhibitions.

people.name: Charles Goodyear Jr.
people.bio: American inventor and son of the rubber pioneer. He built the machine that sews a welt to the upper, which became the basis of the dress shoe trade.

milestones.event: Built a machine that sews a welt to the upper and the insole; the Goodyear welt takes its name from it.

people.name: Thomas Goodwin Green
people.bio: English potter who began the pottery firm that made Cornishware. The firm kept his name, and in 1924 it launched the kitchen range with blue bands on a white ground.

milestones.event: Began the pottery firm in Boston, Lincolnshire.
His firm launched the kitchen range with blue bands that gained the name Cornishware.

people.name: Vasily Perov
people.bio: Russian painter of scenes from the lives of poor people and of the clergy. He was one of the founders of the Peredvizhniki.

milestones.event: Co-founded the Society for Travelling Art Exhibitions.

people.name: William Morris
nationality: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
people.bio: English designer, writer and socialist who made the handmade room a political idea and founded the Arts and Crafts movement.

milestones.event: Moved into the Red House, designed with Philip Webb and furnished by hand.
Founded the decorating firm Morris, Marshall, Faulkner and Co.
Morris, Marshall, Faulkner and Co. sold the adjustable Morris chair and the Sussex chair, c. 1865–66, made in small workshops with plain oak and rush.
Took sole control of the firm, renamed Morris and Co.
Founded the Kelmscott Press.

people.name: Ernest Chaplet
people.bio: French studio potter who made high-fired stoneware with copper-red and flambé glazes. He is a forerunner of the French art pottery of 1900.

people.name: Thomas Burberry
people.bio: English outfitter. He opened a shop at Basingstoke in 1856 and made gabardine in 1879, the cloth of the trench coat.

milestones.event: Opened an outfitter's shop at Basingstoke.
Made gabardine, a rain cloth woven from proofed yarn.
His firm adapted the army officer's raincoat for the war, and the coat became the trench coat.

people.name: Charles Eastlake
nationality: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
people.bio: English architect and writer whose advice book on household taste gave a simpler line to the late Victorian room.

milestones.event: Published Hints on Household Taste.

people.name: Jules Chéret
people.bio: French lithographer who made the colour poster a street art.

milestones.event: Started a period of lithography training in London.
Sold his lithography company to Imprimerie Chaix and became its artistic director.

people.name: Caroline Reboux
people.bio: French milliner who ran one of the best-known hat houses of Paris from 1865, in the years when the poke bonnet gave way to the small hat.

milestones.event: Opened her millinery house in the rue de la Paix, Paris.

people.name: Ivan Kramskoi
people.bio: Russian painter and critic. He led the artists who left the Academy in 1863, and he was the main organiser of the Peredvizhniki.

milestones.event: Led thirteen other students out of the Imperial Academy of Arts in Saint Petersburg.
Helped to found the Society for Travelling Art Exhibitions.

people.name: Benjamin Day Jr.
people.bio: American illustrator who invented the Ben Day dot process for tone and colour.

milestones.event: Developed the Ben Day process of dot patterns.

people.name: Paul Cézanne
people.bio: French painter. Vollard bought about 150 of his canvases for the show of 1895.

photo.credit: Unknown; Cézanne was born in 1839 and died in 1906

milestones.event: First Cézanne show at Vollard's gallery.

people.name: William De Morgan
people.bio: English potter and tile maker. He worked on lustre glazes in Chelsea and Fulham from 1872, and he made vases and tiles with fish, birds and plants in ruby and gold lustre.

milestones.event: Opened a pottery in Chelsea and started to work on lustre glazes.
Began to make hand-painted tiles with plant and animal motifs in Chelsea.
Moved his pottery to Sands End in Fulham.

people.name: Claude Monet
people.bio: French painter whose picture gave Impressionism its name.

milestones.event: Painted Impression, Sunrise.
Showed at the first Impressionist exhibition.
Started his Water Lilies paintings.

people.name: T. J. Cobden-Sanderson
nationality: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
people.bio: English bookbinder and printer who ran the Doves Press.

milestones.event: Set up the Doves Bindery in Hammersmith.
Started to throw the Doves Type into the Thames (1913 is the traditional date; his journals give 1916–17).

people.name: Berthe Morisot
people.bio: French painter, a founding member of the Impressionist group.

milestones.event: Showed at the first Impressionist exhibition.

people.name: Karel Klíč
people.bio: Czech painter and inventor. He made the photogravure process that is still in use, from the earlier work of Fox Talbot.

milestones.event: Developed the mature photogravure process, known as the Talbot-Klič process.

people.name: Rafael Guastavino
people.bio: Spanish builder who moved to New York in 1881. His company made thin tile vaults that carried the load of a ceiling, and the vaults of the City Hall subway station are his best known work.

milestones.event: Built the tile vaults of the City Hall station of the New York subway, with Heins and LaFarge.

people.name: Ilya Repin
people.bio: Russian painter of large group scenes and portraits. He became the best known artist of the Peredvizhniki.

milestones.event: Finished Barge Haulers on the Volga.

people.name: Karl Benz
people.bio: German engineer. His three-wheeled Patent-Motorwagen of 1886 is the first car that was built as one machine, not as a carriage with an engine.

milestones.event: Founded Benz & Cie in Mannheim.
Received the patent for the Patent-Motorwagen.
Sold the Velo, the first car made in series.

people.name: Mary Cassatt
people.bio: American painter and printmaker in Paris. She made colour prints with drypoint and aquatint on several plates.

milestones.event: Showed ten colour prints in Paris, made with drypoint and aquatint.

people.name: Ödön Lechner
people.bio: Hungarian architect who looked for a national style. With the Zsolnay factory he made roofs and facades of colourful, frost-proof ceramic with folk ornament.

milestones.event: Completed the Museum of Applied Arts in Budapest, with a roof of Zsolnay tile.
Completed the Royal Postal Savings Bank in Budapest, with ceramic ornament on the roof.

people.name: Auguste Escoffier
people.bio: French chef who ran the kitchens of the Savoy, the Ritz and the Carlton with César Ritz, organised the brigade de cuisine and wrote Le Guide culinaire.

milestones.event: Took charge of the kitchen of the Savoy Hotel in London.
Created the pêche Melba for Nellie Melba.
Published Le Guide culinaire.

people.name: Eusebi Güell
people.bio: Catalan industrialist and the main patron of Gaudí. He commissioned the Palau Güell, Park Güell and the Colònia Güell crypt.

milestones.event: Gaudí began to build the Palau Güell.
Eusebi Güell died in Barcelona.

people.name: Kobayashi Kiyochika
people.bio: Japanese woodblock artist of the Meiji period. His kosen-ga, light-ray pictures, put Western light and shadow on night scenes of Tokyo.

milestones.event: Began to publish kosen-ga, light-ray prints of Tokyo at night.

people.name: Webb C. Ball
people.bio: American jeweller of Cleveland who set the rules for railroad watches. His standard fixed the accuracy and the marking of a watch that a train crew could use.

milestones.event: Became chief time inspector for railroads and set strict watch standards.

people.name: Gustave Caillebotte
people.bio: French painter and collector. His wealth let him buy Impressionist works, pay rent for artists and help to fund their shows.

milestones.event: Bought his first Monet.
Died and left 68 paintings to the state.

people.name: Paul Gauguin
people.bio: French painter and printmaker. In Brittany he painted flat shapes of strong colour with dark outlines, and he then took this style to Tahiti.

milestones.event: Stayed at Pont-Aven in Brittany for the first time.
Painted Vision after the Sermon and led Paul Sérusier in his work at Pont-Aven.
Sailed to Tahiti.

people.name: Raja Ravi Varma
people.bio: Indian painter of gods and legends in an oil style that mixed Indian subjects with European method. He started a lithographic press to sell copies of his paintings.

milestones.event: Founded the Ravi Varma Press in Mumbai to print oleographs of his paintings.

people.name: Maria Longworth Nichols Storer
people.bio: American potter and patron who founded the Rookwood Pottery in Cincinnati in 1880. Her pottery grew into the best known art pottery of the United States.

milestones.event: Founded the Rookwood Pottery in Cincinnati.
Gave the management of the pottery to William Watts Taylor.

people.name: Thomas Twyford
people.bio: Potter of Hanley, Staffordshire. His one-piece Unitas wash-down closet of 1883 made a smooth ceramic WC that was easy to clean.

milestones.event: Patented the Unitas, a pedestal WC pan cast in one piece of ceramic.

people.name: César Ritz
people.bio: Swiss hotelier who managed the Savoy and founded the Ritz in Paris; he gave Escoffier the grand hotel kitchen and its dining room.

milestones.event: Became manager of the Savoy Hotel in London, with Escoffier as chef.
Opened the Hôtel Ritz in Paris.

people.name: Emery Walker
people.bio: English engraver and typographer who advised William Morris and co-founded the Doves Press.

milestones.event: Became a partner in the Doves Press and supervised the Doves Type.
Received a knighthood.

people.name: Ivan Sytin
people.bio: Russian publisher in Moscow. His firm printed cheap popular sheets and books in large runs, and so brought the lubok to a mass market.

milestones.event: Bought a small lithographic shop in Moscow and began to print cheap popular sheets.

people.name: Antoni Gaudí
people.bio: Catalan architect of Modernisme, the Barcelona form of Art Nouveau, with curved stone and mosaic.

milestones.event: Took over the Sagrada Família project in Barcelona.
Began Park Güell in Barcelona, where the benches and roofs carry broken-tile mosaic.
Completed the Casa Batlló in Barcelona.

people.name: Antonio Vanegas Arroyo
people.bio: Mexican publisher in Mexico City. He printed cheap broadsides, songbooks and chapbooks, and he hired José Guadalupe Posada to make their pictures.

people.name: Gertrude Käsebier
people.bio: American photographer of soft-focus portraits and a founder of the Photo-Secession.

milestones.event: Co-founded the Photo-Secession.

people.name: José Guadalupe Posada
people.bio: Mexican printmaker who made thousands of broadside pictures for the Mexico City press of Antonio Vanegas Arroyo. He is the maker of the La Calavera Catrina image.

milestones.event: About this year he made the La Calavera Catrina plate for the Vanegas Arroyo press.

people.name: Anne Cobden-Sanderson
people.bio: British woman who paid for the Doves Press of her husband T. J. Cobden-Sanderson.

milestones.event: She paid for the Doves Press in Hammersmith.

people.name: Inès Gaches-Sarraute
people.bio: French physician and corsetmaker. Alarmed by the effect of tight corsets on the body, she designed a health corset with a straight front, later called the S-bend corset.

milestones.event: Introduced her health corset, later called the S-bend corset, in a book on the corset.

people.name: Sergei Shchukin
people.bio: Moscow textile merchant and collector. He held a large group of Matisse and Picasso works and opened his home to the public in 1909.

milestones.event: Commissioned La Danse and Music from Matisse.

people.name: Erik Werenskiold
people.bio: Norwegian painter and illustrator of Norwegian folk tales.

milestones.event: Started to illustrate the folk tales of Asbjørnsen and Moe.

people.name: Louis Sullivan
people.bio: American architect of the Chicago School. He designed tall steel-frame buildings with a thin terracotta skin and flowing plant ornament in low relief.

milestones.event: Completed the Wainwright Building in St Louis, with red terracotta ornament on a steel frame.
Completed the Guaranty Building in Buffalo, which is covered in terracotta.

people.name: Theodor Kittelsen
people.bio: Norwegian painter of trolls and the Norwegian landscape.

milestones.event: Published the plague drawings Svartedauen.

people.name: Georges Seurat
people.bio: French painter who built pictures from small dots of pure colour and started Neo-Impressionism.

milestones.event: Completed A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte.

people.name: Alphonse Mucha
people.bio: Czech artist whose posters of women in flowing lines became the image of Art Nouveau.

milestones.event: Made the poster Gismonda for Sarah Bernhardt.
Started The Slav Epic.

people.name: Marianne von Werefkin
people.bio: Russian painter in Munich. Her salon was the start of the Neue Künstlervereinigung München.

milestones.event: Helped to found the Neue Künstlervereinigung München.

people.name: René Lalique
people.bio: French jeweller and glass maker. He used horn, enamel and opal as well as gems, and he drew the curved, natural forms of Art Nouveau jewels.

milestones.event: Showed his jewels at the Exposition Universelle in Paris.

people.name: Fridtjof Nansen
people.bio: Norwegian explorer and scientist. His ski and sledge journeys in wool and windproof dress gave a model to the Nordic life of the open air.

milestones.event: Crossed Greenland on skis with a party of five.
Sailed on the Fram towards the North Pole.

people.name: Victor Horta
people.bio: Belgian architect who made the first Art Nouveau houses, with iron and glass that follow the line of a plant.

milestones.event: Completed the Hôtel Tassel in Brussels, the first Art Nouveau house.
Completed the Hôtel Solvay in Brussels, with the furniture, the door handles and the lamps of his own design.
Completed the Maison du Peuple in Brussels.

people.name: Emile Tassel
people.bio: Belgian scientist and professor. He was the client for the Hôtel Tassel by Victor Horta.

milestones.event: Horta began to build the Hôtel Tassel.

people.name: Charles Robert Ashbee
people.bio: English architect and designer. He founded the Guild of Handicraft and drew silver and enamel jewels that the guild made by hand.

milestones.event: Founded the Guild of Handicraft in London.

people.name: George Eumorfopoulos
people.bio: British collector of Chinese ceramics who owned many Tang tomb figures, among them sancai horses and camels. His collection passed to two national museums in 1934.

milestones.event: His collection of Chinese ceramics passed to the British Museum and the Victoria and Albert Museum.

people.name: William Randolph Hearst
people.bio: US publisher. He bought Harper's Bazaar in 1913 and turned it into a thick glossy magazine.

milestones.event: Bought Harper's Bazaar.

people.name: Alexej von Jawlensky
people.bio: Russian painter who worked in Germany. He painted faces and heads in strong colour and bold outline.

milestones.event: Co-founded the Neue Künstlervereinigung München.

people.name: Alfred Stieglitz
people.bio: American photographer and gallerist who led Pictorialism and then turned against it.

milestones.event: Founded the Photo-Secession.
Started Camera Work, a quarterly with photogravure plates.
Took The Steerage.
Published Paul Strand's work in the last issue of Camera Work.

people.name: Paul Sérusier
people.bio: French painter who was a link between Gauguin and the Nabis. He painted The Talisman in 1888 under the guidance of Gauguin.

milestones.event: Painted The Talisman at Pont-Aven. The Nabis took it as the first picture of their group.

people.name: Akseli Gallen-Kallela
people.bio: Finnish painter of the Kalevala epic.

milestones.event: Painted The Defence of the Sampo.
Painted frescoes for the Finnish pavilion at the Paris World Fair.

people.name: Ambroise Vollard
people.bio: Paris dealer and publisher. He held the first Cézanne show in 1895 and the first Picasso show in 1901.

milestones.event: Held the first Cézanne show after he bought about 150 canvases.

people.name: Beatrix Potter
people.bio: English author and illustrator of children's books. She also made fine studies of fungi, and her small, close view of mushrooms and animals suits goblincore.

milestones.event: Had her paper on the spores of fungi read to the Linnean Society of London.

people.name: Wassily Kandinsky
people.bio: Russian painter and theorist who worked in Munich. He moved step by step from landscape to pictures with no object.

milestones.event: Became the first chairman of the Neue Künstlervereinigung München.
Left the Neue Künstlervereinigung München and founded Der Blaue Reiter with Franz Marc.
Published the Blaue Reiter Almanac with Franz Marc.

people.name: Frank Lloyd Wright
people.bio: American architect. Kaufmann commissioned Fallingwater from him in 1934.

milestones.event: Designed Fallingwater, the house over a waterfall in Pennsylvania.
Finished the main house of Fallingwater.

people.name: Hector Guimard
people.bio: French architect who gave Paris its Art Nouveau metro entrances.

milestones.event: Completed the Castel Béranger in Paris.
Designed the cast-iron railings, door handles and stoves of the Castel Béranger.
Designed the first entrances of the Paris Métro.

people.name: Pierre Bonnard
people.bio: French painter of rooms, gardens and people at home. He was a member of the Nabis and kept their rich colour all his life.

milestones.event: Belonged to the Nabis, whose last group show was in this year.

people.name: Édouard Vuillard
people.bio: French painter of quiet rooms, with patterned walls and cloth. He was a member of the Nabis.

milestones.event: Belonged to the Nabis, whose last group show was in this year.

people.name: Émile Bernard
people.bio: French painter who worked with Louis Anquetin on flat colour areas with a dark outline. Gauguin and he made the Synthetist style at Pont-Aven.

milestones.event: Painted Breton Women in the Meadow in flat shapes with dark contours.
Showed with Gauguin at the Café Volpini in Paris.

people.name: Fritz Waerndorfer
people.bio: Austrian entrepreneur and patron of the arts. He financed the founding of the Wiener Werkstätte.

milestones.event: Financed the founding of the Wiener Werkstätte.

people.name: Peter Behrens
people.bio: German architect and designer. He shaped the corporate identity of AEG, from its buildings to its products.

milestones.event: Became artistic consultant of AEG.

people.name: Henri Matisse
people.bio: French painter of the Fauve group. Shchukin, the Steins, Barnes and the Cone sisters were among his early buyers.

milestones.event: Showed Woman with a Hat at the Salon d'Automne with the group later called the Fauves.
Finished Music for Shchukin.

people.name: Maurice Denis
people.bio: French painter and writer who gave the Nabis their theory. He wrote that a picture is first of all a flat surface covered with colours.

milestones.event: Published his definition of Neo-traditionalism in the journal Art et Critique.

people.name: František Kupka
people.bio: Czech painter who worked in Paris. He was one of the first to paint pictures with no subject, in discs, planes and bright colour.

milestones.event: Showed Amorpha: Fugue in Two Colours at the Salon d'Automne in Paris.

people.name: Albert C. Barnes
people.bio: American chemist and collector. He founded the Barnes Foundation in 1922 and bought many Matisse, Renoir and Cézanne works.

milestones.event: The Barnes Foundation received its charter.
Bought Le Bonheur de vivre.

people.name: Cyril Power
people.bio: English architect and artist. He cut linocuts of the Tube, of sport and of the river, with Sybil Andrews.

milestones.event: Helped to found the Grosvenor School of Modern Art in London.

people.name: Edward Johnston
people.bio: British calligrapher whose lettering for the London Underground gave the model of the humanist sans serif.

photo.credit: Unknown - website states copyright is unknown

milestones.event: Published the book Writing & Illuminating & Lettering.
Received the commission for a typeface for the London Underground.

people.name: Piet Mondrian
people.bio: Dutch painter of grids of black lines and primary colours.

milestones.event: Co-founded De Stijl.
Painted his first compositions in red, yellow, blue and black.
Painted Broadway Boogie Woogie in New York.

people.name: Alberto Santos-Dumont
people.bio: Brazilian aviator in Paris. By the account of the Cartier house, he asked for a watch that he could read in flight without a hand on a pocket chain.

milestones.event: By the account of the Cartier house, asked Louis Cartier for a watch to wear on the wrist in flight.

people.name: Condé Montrose Nast
people.bio: US publisher. He bought Vogue in 1909 and made it a fashion magazine for women.

milestones.event: Bought Vogue.

people.name: Robert Wiene
people.bio: German film director of The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari.

milestones.event: Released The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari.

people.name: Gertrude Stein
people.bio: American writer and collector in Paris. With her brother Leo she bought early Matisse and Picasso works from 1905.

milestones.event: Bought Matisse's Woman with a Hat.
Sat for Picasso's portrait of her.

people.name: Jacques Villon
people.bio: French painter and printmaker, brother of Marcel Duchamp. He gave the Section d'Or its name.

milestones.event: Suggested the name Section d'Or for the group and its show.

people.name: Louis Cartier
people.bio: French jeweller who ran the house of Cartier. He made the wristwatch a gentleman's piece with the Santos and the Tank.

milestones.event: Moved the family house to the rue de la Paix in Paris, where it made garland-style jewels in platinum.
By the account of the Cartier house, made a wristwatch for the aviator Alberto Santos-Dumont.
Drew the Tank, a rectangular watch with straight lugs that follow the lines of the case.

people.name: Walter J. Kohler Sr.
people.bio: American businessman and Governor of Wisconsin. He led the Kohler Co. as president from 1905 to 1937, in the years when its bath fittings were sold in colour.

milestones.event: Became president of the Kohler Co., a maker of baths and sanitary fittings.

people.name: August Sander
people.bio: German portrait photographer who recorded the people of his country by trade and class in a frontal, plain manner.

milestones.event: Published the portrait book Antlitz der Zeit.

people.name: Ivan Bilibin
people.bio: Russian illustrator of the World of Art circle. His fairy-tale books joined a firm black outline, flat tints and folk ornament into one page.

milestones.event: Drew the first of his Russian fairy-tale picture books for the state paper printing works.
Drew cartoons for satirical magazines in St Petersburg.

people.name: Madeleine Vionnet
people.bio: French couturière. She drew her gowns on a small wooden doll and made the bias cut the base of the draped dress of the 1930s.

milestones.event: Opened her own house in Paris.
Closed her house at the start of the war.

people.name: Pyotr Konchalovsky
people.bio: Russian painter of still lifes and landscapes in heavy colour. He was the first chairman of the Jack of Diamonds.

milestones.event: Was elected chairman of the Jack of Diamonds.

people.name: Yoshida Hiroshi
people.bio: Japanese painter and printmaker. He ran his own print workshop and made shin-hanga landscapes of many places in Japan and abroad.

milestones.event: Began to print and publish in his own studio.

people.name: Gabriele Münter
people.bio: German painter of landscapes and portraits in flat colour with strong outlines. She worked with Kandinsky and kept many of his works.

milestones.event: Showed in the first exhibition of Der Blaue Reiter.

people.name: Paul Renner
people.bio: German typeface designer who drew Futura from simple geometric forms.

milestones.event: Designed the typeface Futura for the Bauer foundry.
Published the book Die Kunst der Typographie.

people.name: Edward Steichen
people.bio: Luxembourg-American photographer who moved from Pictorialism to modern fashion photography.

milestones.event: Took The Pond—Moonlight.
Curated The Family of Man at MoMA.

people.name: Émile-Jacques Ruhlmann
people.bio: French furniture maker and decorator whose veneered, ivory-inlaid rooms set the standard of Art Deco luxury.

milestones.event: Founded the firm Ruhlmann et Laurent in Paris.
Showed the Hôtel du Collectionneur pavilion at the Paris exposition of decorative arts.
Furnished the Hôtel du Collectionneur with cabinets, chairs and lamps in ebony and ivory.

people.name: Kazimir Malevich
people.bio: Russian painter who founded Suprematism. In 1923 he designed the form of a white teapot for the State Porcelain Factory, and his pupils painted the first Suprematist cups.

milestones.event: Introduced Suprematism and showed Black Square at the exhibition 0,10 in Petrograd.
Designed the form of the Suprematist teapot for the State Porcelain Factory in Petrograd.

people.name: Bruno Taut
people.bio: German architect who drew glass buildings as a dream of a new society. He started the Glass Chain letters in 1919.

milestones.event: Built the Glass Pavilion for the Werkbund show in Cologne.
Started the Glass Chain, a chain of letters and drawings among architects.

people.name: Ernst Ludwig Kirchner
people.bio: German painter who helped found the group Die Brücke and painted with harsh colour and jagged line.

milestones.event: Founded the artists group Die Brücke in Dresden with three other students.
Cut the Programm der Brücke as a woodcut.

people.name: Franz Marc
people.bio: German painter of animals in bright, simple planes of colour. He founded Der Blaue Reiter with Kandinsky.

milestones.event: Co-founded Der Blaue Reiter.
Published the Blaue Reiter Almanac with Kandinsky.

people.name: Frederick Hurten Rhead
people.bio: English-born potter and art director of the Homer Laughlin company. He designed the Fiesta line and its solid colours.

milestones.event: Launched the Fiesta line in Pittsburgh in solid glaze colours.

people.name: Fritz Bleyl
people.bio: German architect and painter. He was one of the four students who founded Die Brücke.

milestones.event: Co-founded Die Brücke in Dresden.

people.name: Albert Gleizes
people.bio: French painter and theorist of Cubism. He was a leading member of the Puteaux group.

milestones.event: Published Du Cubisme with Jean Metzinger.

people.name: Claude Flight
people.bio: English artist who taught and promoted the colour linocut. He saw it as a cheap and democratic art form.

milestones.event: Organised the first exhibition of British linocuts at the Redfern Gallery in London.

people.name: Henri Le Fauconnier
people.bio: French painter of the early Cubist group. He took part in the shows of the Puteaux circle.

milestones.event: Showed in the Cubist room at the Salon des Indépendants.

people.name: Ilya Mashkov
people.bio: Russian painter of large still lifes in bold colour. He was a founder of the Jack of Diamonds.

milestones.event: Was elected secretary of the Jack of Diamonds.

people.name: Lu Xun
people.bio: Chinese writer. He urged young artists to learn the woodcut of Europe, and he organised classes in Shanghai that began the modern woodcut movement.

milestones.event: Urged young artists to learn the European woodcut and organised a woodcut class in Shanghai.

people.name: Mikhail Larionov
people.bio: Russian painter who named the Jack of Diamonds. He started Rayonism, a style of lines that stand for rays of light.

milestones.event: Named the group Jack of Diamonds.
Published the Rayonist manifesto with Natalia Goncharova.

people.name: Natalia Goncharova
people.bio: Russian painter and designer. She worked with Larionov on Rayonism and drew on Russian folk art.

milestones.event: Left the Jack of Diamonds with Larionov.
Published the Rayonist manifesto with Mikhail Larionov.

people.name: Pablo Picasso
people.bio: Spanish painter who started Cubism with Georges Braque.

milestones.event: Painted Les Demoiselles d'Avignon.
Painted Guernica.
Began to make ceramics at the Madoura pottery in Vallauris.
Settled in Vallauris and made altered vases, plates and plaques in editions.

people.name: Paul Rosenberg
people.bio: Paris dealer. He was the exclusive dealer of Picasso from 1918, Braque from 1922, Léger from 1927 and Matisse from 1936.

milestones.event: Began as exclusive dealer of Picasso.
Began as exclusive dealer of Braque.

people.name: Raymond Hood
people.bio: American architect of Art Deco skyscrapers in New York.

milestones.event: Completed the American Radiator Building in New York.
Completed the McGraw-Hill Building in New York, clad in blue-green glazed terracotta.
Completed 30 Rockefeller Plaza as lead architect.

people.name: Wenzel Hablik
people.bio: German painter and architect who drew crystal cities and flying settlements. He took part in the Glass Chain.

milestones.event: Joined the Glass Chain letters of Bruno Taut.

people.name: George Barbier
people.bio: French illustrator whose fashion plates were coloured by hand through stencils.

milestones.event: Started to write and draw for the Gazette du Bon Ton.
Published the almanac Falbalas et Fanfreluches.

people.name: Georges Braque
people.bio: French painter who started Cubism with Pablo Picasso.

milestones.event: Painted Houses at L'Estaque.
Made the first papier collé.

people.name: Hugo Häring
people.bio: German architect who argued that a building should grow from its use, not from a fixed geometry. He ran the secretariat of Der Ring.

milestones.event: Was elected secretary of Der Ring in Berlin.
Took part in the founding of CIAM at La Sarraz.

people.name: Umberto Boccioni
people.bio: Italian painter and sculptor who was the main painter of Futurism and a writer of its manifesto.

milestones.event: Read the Manifesto of Futurist Painters in Turin.
Completed the sculpture Unique Forms of Continuity in Space.

people.name: Yamamoto Kanae
people.bio: Japanese artist who cut and printed his own blocks. His print Fisherman of 1904 is the start of the sosaku-hanga movement.

milestones.event: Made the print Fisherman, the first work of the sosaku-hanga movement.

people.name: Erich Heckel
people.bio: German painter and printmaker. He was a founder of Die Brücke and cut woodcuts with sharp, flat shapes.

milestones.event: Helped to found Die Brücke in Dresden.

people.name: Gabrielle Chanel
people.bio: French couturière. She put jersey, the straight chemise and the short skirt into couture, made costume jewellery a fashion, and in 1955 launched the quilted flap bag on a chain.

milestones.event: Opened a hat shop in Paris.
Showed day dresses in jersey, a cloth that men used for underwear.
Wore long ropes of imitation pearls and large false jewels with her day clothes, and made them the fashion.
Showed a short black crêpe dress that American Vogue compared to the Ford car.
Launched the quilted bag with a chain strap, named for its month and year.

people.name: Jean Metzinger
people.bio: French painter and writer who made Cubist pictures of many views. He wrote Du Cubisme with Albert Gleizes.

milestones.event: Published Du Cubisme with Albert Gleizes.

people.name: Kawase Hasui
people.bio: Japanese landscape designer of shin-hanga prints. He made views of rain, snow and night for the Watanabe shop.

milestones.event: Began to design prints for the Watanabe shop.

people.name: Necmeddin Okyay
people.bio: Turkish artist who taught ebru at the Fine Arts Academy in Istanbul. He brought the craft back into use in the twentieth century. Sources give 1883 or 1885 as his birth year.

people.name: Theo van Doesburg
people.bio: Dutch artist who founded the magazine De Stijl and spread its ideas across Europe.

milestones.event: Founded the magazine De Stijl.
Started Elementarism and added the diagonal.

people.name: Walter Gropius
people.bio: German architect who founded the Bauhaus school and later taught modern architecture at Harvard.

milestones.event: Founded the Bauhaus in Weimar.
The Bauhaus opened a pottery workshop at Dornburg; its students later shaped porcelain for factory production.
Completed the Bauhaus building in Dessau.
Started to teach at the Harvard Graduate School of Design.

people.name: William Van Alen
people.bio: American architect of the Chrysler Building, the tallest Art Deco tower of its day.

milestones.event: Completed the Chrysler Building in New York.
Wore a costume of his building at the Beaux-Arts Ball in New York.

people.name: Karl Schmidt-Rottluff
people.bio: German painter and printmaker, known for strong colour and heavy woodcuts. He was a founder of Die Brücke.

milestones.event: Co-founded Die Brücke in Dresden.

people.name: Edgar Kaufmann
people.bio: Pittsburgh department store owner. He commissioned Fallingwater from Frank Lloyd Wright in 1934.

milestones.event: Hired Wright to design Fallingwater.

people.name: Robert Delaunay
people.bio: French painter who moved from Cubism to bright, abstract colour. He called his method simultaneous contrast of colour.

milestones.event: Painted Simultaneous Windows on the City.

people.name: Sonia Delaunay
people.bio: Painter and designer born in Ukraine. She worked with Robert Delaunay on discs of colour, in pictures, books and cloth.

milestones.event: Made a long colour book with the poet Blaise Cendrars.
Painted Prismes électriques.

people.name: Watanabe Shozaburo
people.bio: Japanese print publisher in Tokyo. He revived the ukiyo-e split of designer, carver and printer, and led the shin-hanga movement.

milestones.event: Coined the term shin-hanga, new prints, for his revival of the woodblock print.

people.name: Edward Weston
people.bio: American photographer of sharp still lifes and landscapes, a founder of Group f/64.

milestones.event: Took Pepper No. 30.
Co-founded Group f/64.

people.name: Elena König Scavini
people.bio: Italian founder of Lenci in Turin in 1919. The firm made felt dolls first and, from the late 1920s, glazed earthenware figures with a deco look.

milestones.event: Founded Lenci in Turin.

people.name: George Mallory
people.bio: English mountaineer. He went to Everest in 1921, 1922 and 1924, and died on the mountain in layers of wool and silk under a gabardine smock.

milestones.event: Went to Everest with the first reconnaissance party.
Took part in the second Everest expedition.
Died near the summit of Everest in layers of wool, silk and gabardine.

people.name: Heorhiy Narbut
people.bio: Ukrainian graphic artist. He drew covers, heraldry and lettering in a Baroque style, and he taught graphic art in Kyiv.

milestones.event: Became a professor of graphic art at the new Ukrainian Academy of Arts in Kyiv.
Designed banknotes and postage stamps in Kyiv for the Ukrainian State.

people.name: Ludwig Mies van der Rohe
people.bio: German-American architect of steel and glass, and the last director of the Bauhaus.

milestones.event: Completed the Barcelona Pavilion.
Became director of the Bauhaus.
Completed the Seagram Building in New York.

people.name: August Macke
people.bio: German painter of city streets, gardens and shop windows in clear, light colour. He belonged to the Blaue Reiter circle.

milestones.event: Joined the Blaue Reiter circle.

people.name: Bernard Leach
people.bio: English potter who learnt in Japan and started a pottery at St Ives with Shōji Hamada in 1920. His book A Potter's Book of 1940 taught studio pottery to a generation.

milestones.event: Founded the Leach Pottery at St Ives with Shōji Hamada.
Published A Potter's Book.

people.name: Erich Mendelsohn
people.bio: German architect who shaped buildings as single sculpted forms, best known for the Einstein Tower.

milestones.event: Began the construction of the Einstein Tower, a solar observatory in Potsdam.

people.name: Hermann Finsterlin
people.bio: German architect, painter and composer who drew free, shell-like buildings. He took part in the Glass Chain.

milestones.event: Joined the Glass Chain letters of Bruno Taut.

people.name: Kazuchika Okura
people.bio: Japanese industrialist who led the start of Toyo Toki in 1917, the company that became Toto. It built the sanitary ware business that launched the Washlet.

milestones.event: Led the start of Toyo Toki, the company that became Toto.

people.name: Le Corbusier
people.bio: Swiss-French architect who wrote the five points of a new architecture and used raw concrete in his late work.

milestones.event: Published Vers une architecture.
Completed the Villa Savoye in Poissy.
Completed the Unité d'Habitation in Marseille, in béton brut.

people.name: Marcel Duchamp
people.bio: French and American artist. He painted in the Cubist manner before he turned to the ready-made.

milestones.event: Painted Nude Descending a Staircase No. 2.
Showed it at the Armory Show in New York.

people.name: F. W. Murnau
people.bio: German film director of Nosferatu.

milestones.event: Released Nosferatu.
Released The Last Laugh.

people.name: Sigfried Giedion
people.bio: Swiss historian and critic who spoke for modern architecture. He was the first secretary-general of CIAM.

milestones.event: Became the first secretary-general of CIAM at La Sarraz.
Published Space, Time and Architecture.

people.name: Marcel Boussac
people.bio: French textile businessman. His group Boussac Saint-Frères paid for the Dior couture house in 1946 and held the majority.

milestones.event: Paid for the Dior couture house at 30 Avenue Montaigne.

people.name: Paul Jaray
people.bio: Engineer born in Vienna. He worked on airship hulls and then used wind-tunnel tests to shape the body of a car.

milestones.event: Joined the Zeppelin airship works in Friedrichshafen.
Patented a streamlined car body.

people.name: P. V. H. Weems
people.bio: American naval officer and navigation teacher. He designed the Hour Angle watch for pilots with the help of Charles Lindbergh.

milestones.event: Designed the Hour Angle watch for long-distance navigation, made by Longines.

people.name: Yanagi Sōetsu
people.bio: Japanese philosopher and art critic who founded the mingei movement. He praised the plain daily pots of unknown village potters and worked with Hamada Shōji and Kawai Kanjirō.

milestones.event: Made his first visit to Korea and began to collect Joseon pottery.
Wrote the prospectus for a museum of folk crafts with Hamada Shōji and Kawai Kanjirō, and used the word mingei.
Opened the Japan Folk Crafts Museum in Tokyo.

people.name: Carl Krayl
people.bio: German architect who took part in the Glass Chain and later in Der Ring. He built housing in Magdeburg.

milestones.event: Joined the Glass Chain letters of Bruno Taut.
Joined Der Ring in Berlin.

people.name: El Lissitzky
people.bio: Russian artist and designer of Constructivist books and exhibitions.

milestones.event: Made the poster Beat the Whites with the Red Wedge.
Designed the book For the Voice.
Designed the photomontage frieze of the Soviet pavilion at the Pressa fair in Cologne.

people.name: Fritz Lang
people.bio: Austrian-German film director of Metropolis and M.

milestones.event: Released the film Metropolis.
Released the film M.

people.name: Mikhail Cheremnykh
people.bio: Russian poster artist and caricaturist. He started the ROSTA Windows in Moscow and led the team of artists that made them.

milestones.event: Drew the first ROSTA Window in Moscow and led the team that made the later windows.

people.name: Paul Strand
people.bio: American photographer whose sharp, direct pictures defined straight photography.
