milestones.event: Took Blind Woman in New York.
His work filled the last issue of Camera Work.

people.name: Alexander Rodchenko
people.bio: Russian artist who made Constructivist posters, photographs and typography.

milestones.event: Signed the Constructivist programme and left easel painting.
Made the Books poster with Lilya Brik.
Designed the poster Books, with a photograph of Lilya Brik, for a state publisher.

people.name: Caresse Crosby
people.bio: American socialite and publisher, born Mary Phelps Jacob. She patented the backless brassière, a light band of two handkerchiefs and ribbon that did not need a corset.

milestones.event: Filed a patent for the backless brassière on 12 February.
Received the first US patent in the new class of brassières on 3 November, and later sold the patent to the Warner Brothers Corset Company.

people.name: Gio Ponti
people.bio: Italian architect and designer. He worked with Italian tile makers on blue and white and green and white tile patterns for walls and floors, in the years when Italian tiles became an industry.

milestones.event: Began to design tile patterns for Ceramica D'Agostino, used in the Parco dei Principi hotels.

people.name: Onchi Koshiro
people.bio: Japanese artist and a leader of abstract woodblock art. He cut and printed his own blocks and made one of the first abstract prints in Japan.

milestones.event: Helped to found the magazine Tsukuhae with Fujimori and Tanaka.

people.name: Raymond Templier
people.bio: French jeweller of a Paris family firm. He drew hard, geometric jewels in platinum, diamond and black onyx.

milestones.event: Showed geometric jewels at the Exposition des Arts Décoratifs in Paris.

people.name: Percival David
people.bio: British collector of Chinese ceramics. His collection holds some of the finest Ding ware outside China.

milestones.event: Gave his collection of Chinese ceramics to the University of London.

people.name: Richard Neutra
people.bio: Austrian-American architect of glass houses in the California landscape.

milestones.event: Completed the Lovell Health House in Los Angeles.
Completed the Kaufmann Desert House in Palm Springs.

people.name: Battista Pininfarina
people.bio: Italian coachbuilder. He founded his Turin workshop in 1930 and made clean, low car bodies that became the model of the grand tourer.

milestones.event: Founded the Carrozzeria Pinin Farina in Turin.
Built the Cisitalia 202 coupe, with the wings joined into the body.
The Museum of Modern Art in New York showed the Cisitalia 202.

people.name: Hans Scharoun
people.bio: German architect who built free, flowing plans from the way people use a room. He took part in the Glass Chain and in Der Ring.

milestones.event: Wrote to the Glass Chain circle of Bruno Taut.
Completed the Berlin Philharmonie.

people.name: Harley Earl
people.bio: American designer. He led styling at General Motors from 1927, and he added the tail fin, the wrap-around glass and the dream car to the car trade.

milestones.event: Started the Art and Colour Section at General Motors.
Put the first tail fins on a Cadillac.
Opened the Motorama show of dream cars.

people.name: Marianne Brandt
people.bio: German designer of Bauhaus metal objects and lamps.

milestones.event: Designed the MT49 tea infuser.
Became head of the Bauhaus metal workshop.

people.name: Raymond Loewy
people.bio: French-born American industrial designer who gave trains, refrigerators and small appliances a smooth, rounded shell.

milestones.event: Drew a streamlined pencil sharpener to show that a small object can carry a teardrop shell.
Redesigned the Coldspot refrigerator with a rounded body and a flush door.

people.name: Vladimir Mayakovsky
people.bio: Russian poet and artist. He drew the panels and wrote the rhymed captions of many ROSTA Windows, and he led the LEF group.

milestones.event: Drew panels and wrote the verse captions of ROSTA Windows in Moscow.
Led the group that published the journal LEF.

people.name: Edward VIII
people.bio: King of the United Kingdom in 1936. As Prince of Wales he set the model of men's country dress: Fair Isle jumpers, plus-fours and strong tweed checks.

emblem.credit: Wikimedia Commons contributors; see the file page

milestones.event: Wore a Fair Isle jumper to play golf, and the knit became a fashion.

people.name: John Ford
people.bio: American director who gave clear story, light and cut to the studio-era film.

milestones.event: Released Stagecoach.
Released The Searchers.

people.name: Dorothea Lange
people.bio: American photographer whose pictures of farm workers and migrants in the 1930s made the case for relief.

milestones.event: Took Migrant Mother for the Resettlement Administration.

people.name: Gustavs Klucis
people.bio: Latvian-born Soviet artist. He built posters from cut photographs and flat shapes, and his montages set the look of the Soviet photomontage poster.

milestones.event: Designed the poster Under the Banner of Lenin for Socialist Construction.
Made a poster of agricultural shock workers from cut photographs.

people.name: Jean Saudé
people.bio: French printmaker in Paris who ran a pochoir workshop and wrote the guide to the method.

milestones.event: Published the guide Traité d'enluminure d'art au pochoir.

people.name: László Moholy-Nagy
people.bio: Hungarian artist and teacher who brought photography and typography into the Bauhaus.

milestones.event: Started to teach the preliminary course at the Bauhaus.
Founded the New Bauhaus in Chicago.

people.name: Serizawa Keisuke
people.bio: Japanese dyer and designer of the mingei movement. He used the katazome stencil for pictorial work on cloth, not only for repeat patterns.

people.name: Dziga Vertov
people.bio: Soviet documentary director of the Kino-Eye.

milestones.event: Released Man with a Movie Camera.

people.name: Wallace Carothers
people.bio: American chemist who led organic chemistry research at DuPont and is credited with the invention of nylon, the fibre of the stocking and the girdle.

milestones.event: Led the DuPont team that made the first nylon polymer.

people.name: Walter Paepcke
people.bio: American businessman who led the Container Corporation of America. He hired Herbert Bayer and founded the International Design Conference in Aspen.

milestones.event: Hired Herbert Bayer and brought him to Aspen.
Founded the International Design Conference in Aspen.

people.name: Warren Marrison
people.bio: Canadian-born American engineer at Bell Telephone Laboratories. In 1927 he built the first quartz clock, the root of the quartz watch.

milestones.event: Built the first quartz clock at Bell Telephone Laboratories.

people.name: Fernand Point
people.bio: French restaurateur and cook of La Pyramide in Vienne. He trained many chefs of the next generation, among them Paul Bocuse, the Troisgros brothers and Alain Chapel.

milestones.event: Took over his father's restaurant in Vienne and named it La Pyramide.
La Pyramide won three Michelin stars.
Died in Vienne.

people.name: Mikhail Kaufman
people.bio: Soviet camera operator and the brother of Dziga Vertov. He was one of the three Kinoks and the cameraman of Man with a Movie Camera.

milestones.event: Shot Man with a Movie Camera for his brother.

people.name: Alvar Aalto
people.bio: Finnish architect and designer of bent plywood furniture.

milestones.event: Designed the Paimio armchair of bent birch plywood.
Completed the Paimio Sanatorium and its Paimio chair.
Founded Artek.

people.name: Fulco di Verdura
people.bio: Sicilian duke and jewel designer. He drew gold and gem jewels for Chanel, and then made warm, sculpted clips and cuffs with large stones.

milestones.event: Opened his own jewellery house in New York.

people.name: Peggy Guggenheim
people.bio: American collector. She opened Art of This Century in New York in 1942 and signed Pollock to a gallery contract in 1943.

milestones.event: Opened Art of This Century.
Signed a gallery contract with Pollock.

people.name: René Magritte
people.bio: Belgian Surrealist painter who set calm, odd objects and text under pictures. Surreal memes use the same flat, deadpan unease. In 1937 he stayed with Edward James in London.

photo.credit: Unknown author Restored by Giovanni Cardinali

milestones.event: Painted The Treachery of Images, a pipe above the words that deny it.
Painted two portraits of Edward James.
Painted The Son of Man.

people.name: Salvatore Ferragamo
people.bio: Italian shoemaker. He made shoes for film and stage in California, then in Florence, and he tried many new lasts, heels and soles.

milestones.event: Opened a shop in Hollywood and made custom shoes for film dancers and stars.
Made the Rainbow sandal with a raised, covered wedge sole, a forerunner of the platform shoe.

people.name: Sergei Eisenstein
people.bio: Soviet film director and theorist of montage.

milestones.event: Released Battleship Potemkin.
Released October.

people.name: Sybil Andrews
people.bio: English-Canadian artist known for modernist colour linocuts. She worked with Cyril Power for many years, and they shared a studio from 1930 to 1938.

milestones.event: About 1926, cut her first linocuts, after the classes of Claude Flight.

people.name: Alfred Hitchcock
people.bio: English director who played with hidden cuts to make a film seem like one shot.

milestones.event: Released Rope.

people.name: Clarice Cliff
people.bio: English ceramic painter. At the Newport Pottery in Burslem she designed bold, hand-painted patterns in bright colours on white earthenware.

milestones.event: Launched the Bizarre range of bright, hand-painted ware at the Newport Pottery in Burslem.

people.name: Eddie Bauer
people.bio: American outdoorsman. He opened a sports shop in Seattle in 1920 and in 1936 made the first quilted down jacket.

milestones.event: Opened a sporting goods shop in Seattle.
Made the first quilted jacket with box baffles of goose down.
Made down flight parkas for the US Army Air Forces.

people.name: Lev Kuleshov
people.bio: Soviet film theorist who showed that a cut makes meaning.

milestones.event: Founded his workshop at the Moscow Film School.
Made the editing experiment now called the Kuleshov effect.

people.name: Weegee
people.bio: American press photographer who shot New York crime scenes at night with hard flash light.

milestones.event: Left Acme Newspictures to work as a freelance photographer.
Published the book Naked City.

people.name: Elizaveta Svilova
people.bio: Soviet film editor and director. She was the partner of Dziga Vertov and a member of the Kinoks. She cut Man with a Movie Camera.

milestones.event: Edited Man with a Movie Camera.

people.name: Hang Zhiying
people.bio: Chinese painter of Shanghai calendar posters (yuefenpai). He drew the young women for advertisers in rubbed charcoal and watercolour.

people.name: Herbert Bayer
people.bio: Austrian-American designer who made the Bauhaus typography and its single-case alphabet.

milestones.event: Designed the Universal alphabet at the Bauhaus.
Moved to the United States and curated the Bauhaus show at MoMA.

people.name: William Haines
people.bio: American film actor who became the decorator of the Hollywood stars and gave Regency forms a glamorous film-set finish.

milestones.event: Completed the interiors of Sunnylands, the Annenberg estate in Rancho Mirage.

people.name: A. M. Cassandre
people.bio: French poster artist and type designer of the Art Deco period.

milestones.event: Made the Étoile du Nord railway poster.
Made the Normandie liner poster.

people.name: Chuck Taylor
people.bio: American basketball player and salesman. He taught the game with the canvas shoe and gave it his name.

milestones.event: His name went on the ankle patch of the canvas basketball shoe, which sold under it for decades.

people.name: Jean Prouvé
people.bio: French metalworker, designer and engineer who made furniture and lamps of bent and welded steel for schools, offices and factories.

milestones.event: Designed the Standard chair of pressed and welded steel.
Designed the Potence wall lamp with a swivel arm of steel tube.

people.name: Ansel Adams
people.bio: American photographer of the American West and inventor of the Zone System.

milestones.event: Co-founded Group f/64.
Took Moonrise, Hernandez, New Mexico.

people.name: Arne Jacobsen
people.bio: Danish architect and designer of the Ant, Egg and Swan chairs.

milestones.event: Designed the Ant chair.
Completed the SAS Royal Hotel in Copenhagen.

people.name: Charles Lindbergh
people.bio: American aviator who flew solo across the Atlantic in 1927. He took part in the design of a watch that a pilot could use to find the longitude.

milestones.event: Took part in the design of the Hour Angle watch with P. V. H. Weems.

people.name: Josep Lluís Sert
people.bio: Catalan architect who worked with Le Corbusier and then taught in the United States. He was president of CIAM from 1947 to 1956.

milestones.event: Co-founded the GATCPAC group in Barcelona.
Became president of CIAM.

people.name: Leopoldo Méndez
people.bio: Mexican printmaker. He helped to found the Taller de Gráfica Popular and led its work in linocut and woodcut.

milestones.event: Helped to found the Taller de Gráfica Popular in Mexico City.

people.name: Lucie Rie
people.bio: Austrian-born potter who worked in London from 1938. She made thin porcelain and stoneware bowls and bottles with pitted glazes and fine scratched lines. Hans Coper worked with her from 1946.

milestones.event: Left Vienna and settled in London as a potter.
Started to work with Hans Coper in her studio at Albion Mews.

people.name: Marcel Breuer
people.bio: Hungarian-American architect and furniture designer of tubular steel chairs.

milestones.event: Designed the Wassily chair.
Completed the Whitney Museum building in New York.

people.name: Marie-Laure de Noailles
people.bio: French patron. With her husband she paid for four avant-garde works in 1929 and 1930, among them L'Âge d'Or.

milestones.event: Paid for L'Âge d'Or.

people.name: Charles Arpels
people.bio: French jeweller of the house Van Cleef & Arpels. In 1933 his firm registered the minaudière, a rigid evening case with compartments.

milestones.event: Registered the minaudière, a rigid evening case with compartments, at Van Cleef & Arpels.

people.name: Edith Farnsworth
people.bio: American physician. She asked Mies van der Rohe to design the Farnsworth House in 1945.

milestones.event: Asked Mies to design a weekend house.

people.name: Margaret De Patta
people.bio: American jeweller and teacher. She made small abstract jewels by hand from silver and cut stones, with ideas from modern art.

milestones.event: Studied under László Moholy-Nagy in Chicago, and then made abstract jewels at the bench.

people.name: Mark Rothko
people.bio: American painter of large soft fields of colour.

milestones.event: Painted his first colour-field works.
The Rothko Chapel opened in Houston.

people.name: Arthur Kneibler
people.bio: American designer at Coopers, Inc. of Kenosha. He designed the first Y-front brief, with a short leg, an elastic waist and an overlapping Y-shaped fly.

milestones.event: Designed the Y-front brief for Coopers, Inc.
Saw the first briefs go on sale at a store in Chicago on 19 January; the shop sold over 30,000 pairs in three months.

people.name: Isamu Noguchi
people.bio: Japanese-American sculptor and designer who joined Japanese craft and modern design.

milestones.event: Designed the Noguchi table for Herman Miller.
Designed the first Akari paper lamps.
Joined Japanese paper and bamboo craft to modern form in the first Akari lamps.

people.name: Robert Montgomery
people.bio: An American actor and director. He directed Lady in the Lake (1947), a film shot from the point of view of its main character.

milestones.event: Directed Lady in the Lake, a feature film shot almost all through the eyes of its main character.

people.name: Russel Wright
people.bio: American industrial designer. His American Modern dinnerware set a soft, curved shape and muted glaze colours in the home.

milestones.event: Launched American Modern dinnerware with the Steubenville Pottery.

people.name: Salvador Dalí
people.bio: Spanish Surrealist painter. Edward James and the Noailles couple were among his patrons.

milestones.event: Joined the Surrealist group.
Made L'Âge d'Or with Buñuel.
Completed The Persistence of Memory.
Received a year of financial support from the patron Edward James.

people.name: Willem de Kooning
people.bio: Dutch-American painter of violent gestural brushwork.

milestones.event: Painted Excavation.
Painted Woman I.

people.name: Barnett Newman
people.bio: American painter. Betty Parsons gave him his first solo show in 1950.

milestones.event: First solo show at the Betty Parsons Gallery.

people.name: Christian Dior
people.bio: French couturier. His first collection, in 1947, set the small waist and the full skirt of post-war dress.

milestones.event: Opened his couture house at 30 avenue Montaigne, Paris.
Showed the Corolle line with the Bar suit; Carmel Snow called it the New Look.
Showed the H-line, a straight line with a low waist.

people.name: Howard Hughes
people.bio: US businessman. He spent 8.8 million dollars in 1948 to take control of RKO Pictures.

milestones.event: Took control of RKO Pictures.

people.name: Jiro Yoshihara
people.bio: Japanese painter and businessman. He founded and led the Gutai Art Association.

milestones.event: Founded the Gutai Art Association in Ashiya.
Died, and the Gutai Art Association closed soon after.

people.name: Billy Wilder
people.bio: Austrian-born American director who made definitive film noir works with hard light and a tired narrator.

milestones.event: Directed Double Indemnity with Raymond Chandler.
Directed Sunset Boulevard.

people.name: Carlo Scarpa
people.bio: Italian architect from Venice who set new work against old stone with fine detail in the Castelvecchio museum.

milestones.event: Began the conversion of the Castelvecchio in Verona into a museum.

people.name: Jeon Hyeong-pil
people.bio: Korean collector, called Gansong. He bought Goryeo celadon from dealers in Japanese hands and so kept many of the best pieces in Korea, among them the crane maebyeong.

milestones.event: Bought the celadon maebyeong with inlaid clouds and cranes, now a Korean national treasure.

people.name: Philip Johnson
people.bio: American architect and curator who named the International Style and later turned to Postmodernism.

milestones.event: Curated the Modern Architecture show at MoMA, which named the International Style.
Completed the Glass House in New Canaan.
Completed the AT&T Building in New York, with a broken pediment on top.

people.name: Roberto Rossellini
people.bio: Italian director who made the first neorealist films in real streets with ordinary people.

milestones.event: Released Rome, Open City.
Released Paisà.
Released Germany, Year Zero.

people.name: Altina Schinasi
people.bio: American designer and artist. She drew the Harlequin glasses, the first cat-eye frame, in 1939 and sold them in New York shops.

milestones.event: Designed the Harlequin frame, with raised outer corners, and sold it in New York shops.

people.name: Charles Eames
people.bio: American designer who, with Ray Eames, made moulded plywood and plastic furniture.

milestones.event: Put the moulded plywood chair into production with Ray Eames.
Completed the Eames House in Los Angeles with Ray Eames.
Designed the Eames Lounge Chair with Ray Eames.

people.name: Edward James
people.bio: British collector and patron of the Surrealists. He sponsored Dalí in 1938 and hosted Magritte in 1937.

milestones.event: Hosted Magritte in London.
Sponsored Dalí for the year.

people.name: Roger Vivier
people.bio: French shoe designer. He worked for the couture houses and shaped the thin heel and the pointed court shoe of the 1950s.

milestones.event: Opened his own shoe house in Paris.
Began to make the shoes for the Dior collections, with thin, steel-cored heels.

people.name: Dominique de Menil
people.bio: Houston patron. With her husband John she commissioned the Rothko Chapel in 1964.

milestones.event: Commissioned Rothko to make the chapel paintings.

people.name: George Nelson
people.bio: American designer and design director of Herman Miller.

milestones.event: Became design director of Herman Miller.
Designed the Ball Clock.

people.name: Henri Cartier-Bresson
people.bio: French photographer of the decisive moment and a founder of Magnum.

milestones.event: Co-founded Magnum Photos.
Published Images à la sauvette (The Decisive Moment).

people.name: Lawrence W. Butler
people.bio: Special-effects artist who won an Oscar for the blue-screen travelling matte in The Thief of Bagdad.

milestones.event: Made the travelling-matte effects of The Thief of Bagdad.

people.name: Nicholas Kurti
people.bio: Hungarian-born physicist of Oxford, who argued that cooks should study the physics of food, and who founded the field of molecular gastronomy with Hervé This.

milestones.event: Gave the lecture The Physicist in the Kitchen at the Royal Institution in London.
Co-founded the workshop on molecular and physical gastronomy in Erice with Hervé This.

people.name: Jean Bugatti
people.bio: Son of Ettore Bugatti. He drew the bodies of the Type 57 cars, with a sharp seam along the top of each wing.

milestones.event: Drew the Type 57 Ventoux and Atalante bodies.
Showed the Type 57S Atlantic, with a riveted spine along the roof.

people.name: Luis Arenal
people.bio: Mexican painter and printmaker. He helped to found the Taller de Gráfica Popular.

milestones.event: Helped to found the Taller de Gráfica Popular in Mexico City.

people.name: Eero Saarinen
people.bio: Finnish-American architect and furniture designer of sweeping concrete roofs and the Tulip chair.

milestones.event: Designed the Tulip chair for Knoll.
Completed the TWA Flight Center in New York.

people.name: Eliot Noyes
people.bio: American architect and industrial designer. He led the first corporate-wide design programme at IBM.

milestones.event: Commissioned by Thomas J. Watson Jr. to build the IBM design programme.

people.name: Julius Shulman
people.bio: American photographer whose pictures of modernist houses in California set the way that architecture is shown.

milestones.event: Photographed the Kaufmann House in Palm Springs by Richard Neutra.
Took Case Study House #22, the Stahl House.

people.name: Max Miedinger
people.bio: Swiss type designer who drew Neue Haas Grotesk, later Helvetica.

milestones.event: Drew Neue Haas Grotesk with Eduard Hoffmann.
Neue Haas Grotesk was renamed Helvetica.

people.name: Bill Bowerman
people.bio: American athletics coach at the University of Oregon. He made shoes for his runners by hand and co-founded the company that became Nike.

milestones.event: Co-founded Blue Ribbon Sports to sell running shoes.
Poured rubber into a waffle iron to make a light, grippy sole.

people.name: John Lautner
people.bio: American architect who built bold roofs and glass walls in Los Angeles. His Googie's Coffee Shop gave the style its name.

milestones.event: Designed Googie's Coffee Shop in Hollywood.
Completed the Chemosphere house in Los Angeles.

people.name: Kaj Franck
people.bio: Finnish designer and art director of Arabia. He made a small, modular stacking service from plain shapes.

milestones.event: Launched the Kilta stacking service for Arabia.

people.name: Okamoto Tarō
people.bio: Japanese artist who saw Jōmon pottery as great art, not as an archaeological find. His essay of 1952 changed how Japan and the world looked at the flame-style pots.

milestones.event: Published an essay in the art journal Mizue that praised Jōmon pottery as art.

people.name: Jackson Pollock
people.bio: American painter who poured and dripped paint on canvas laid on the floor.

milestones.event: Started his drip paintings.
Painted Autumn Rhythm.

people.name: Li Qun
people.bio: Chinese woodcut artist of the movement that Lu Xun began. He cut a portrait of Lu Xun in 1936 and worked in Yan'an.

milestones.event: Cut the woodcut Portrait of Lu Xun.

people.name: Ray Eames
people.bio: American artist and designer who, with Charles Eames, made modern furniture and films.

milestones.event: Completed the Eames House in Los Angeles with Charles Eames.
Released the film Powers of Ten with Charles Eames.

people.name: Wilbert L. Gore
people.bio: American engineer. He left a chemical firm in 1958 and founded W. L. Gore and Associates at Newark, Delaware, the firm that made the Gore-Tex membrane.

milestones.event: Founded his firm at Newark, Delaware.
His son Bob stretched a rod of PTFE and made the porous membrane that the firm later sold in Gore-Tex.
His firm sold the first membrane cloth for garments.

people.name: Georges Candilis
people.bio: Greek-French architect who worked with Le Corbusier and then led the Candilis-Josic-Woods office. He was a core member of Team 10.

milestones.event: Won the competition for the Toulouse-Le Mirail new town with Josic and Woods.
Won the competition for the Free University in Berlin with Josic and Woods.

people.name: Kenzo Tange
people.bio: Japanese architect who joined modern concrete to Japanese forms and taught the Metabolists. He drew the Tokyo Bay plan.

milestones.event: Published A Plan for Tokyo 1960, a linear city over Tokyo Bay.
Completed the Yamanashi Press and Broadcasting Center in Kofu.
Planned the whole site of Expo 70 in Osaka.

people.name: Kim Whanki
people.bio: Korean painter who collected Joseon white porcelain and painted the moon jar again and again. His work made the round white jar a symbol of Korean taste in the modern age.

people.name: Asger Jorn
people.bio: Danish painter and writer. He helped to found CoBrA and, later, the Situationist International.

milestones.event: Co-founded CoBrA in Paris.
Co-founded the Situationist International.

people.name: Hans Wegner
people.bio: Danish furniture designer of the Wishbone chair.

milestones.event: Designed The Chair.
Designed the Wishbone chair for Carl Hansen & Søn.
Designed the Wishbone chair of steam-bent ash and a paper cord seat.

people.name: Jaap Bakema
people.bio: Dutch architect and teacher who joined architecture to town planning. He was a core member of Team 10 until his death.

milestones.event: Completed the Lijnbaan shopping street in Rotterdam with Van den Broek.
Took part in the last CIAM congress at Otterlo.

people.name: Josef Müller-Brockmann
people.bio: Swiss graphic designer of grid systems and concert posters.

milestones.event: Made the Der Film poster.
Published Grid Systems in Graphic Design.

people.name: Louis Armet
people.bio: American architect who founded the firm Armet and Davis with Eldon Davis. The firm designed coffee shops in Los Angeles.

milestones.event: Founded Armet and Davis with Eldon Davis in Los Angeles.

people.name: Mario Bava
people.bio: Italian director and cinematographer who made the first giallo films with saturated colour light.

milestones.event: Released The Girl Who Knew Too Much, an early giallo.
Released Blood and Black Lace.

people.name: Paul Rand
people.bio: American graphic designer of corporate logos and playful modern layouts.

milestones.event: Designed the IBM logo.
Designed the Westinghouse logo.

people.name: Klaus Märtens
people.bio: German army doctor. He injured his ankle in 1945 and designed a boot with an air-cushioned sole, the sole of the later workboot.

milestones.event: Injured his ankle skiing and designed boots with air-cushioned soles.
Founded a company at Seeshaupt, Germany, on the sole patent.

people.name: S. Donald Stookey
people.bio: American chemist at Corning. In 1953 he found that a glass left in a furnace at too high a heat turned into a strong glass-ceramic, which led to cookware.

milestones.event: Found glass-ceramic when a furnace overheated a glass plate.
His glass-ceramic became the first white cookware that went from freezer to flame.

people.name: Noboru Hayama
people.bio: Japanese founder of Riso Kagaku, the maker of the Risograph and Print Gocco.

milestones.event: Founded Riso Kagaku in Tokyo.
His company started to sell the Print Gocco kit.

people.name: Ruth Handler
people.bio: American businesswoman and co-founder of Mattel. She created the Barbie doll, the toy that gave Barbiecore its colour and its plastic shine.

milestones.event: Presented the Barbie doll at the American International Toy Fair in New York.

people.name: Eldon Davis
people.bio: American architect of the firm Armet and Davis. He designed coffee shops in Los Angeles with upswept roofs and bright signs.

milestones.event: Completed Norms La Cienega in Los Angeles with Louis Armet.

people.name: Ettore Sottsass
people.bio: Italian architect and designer who founded the Memphis Group.

milestones.event: Designed the red Valentine typewriter for Olivetti.
Designed the Carlton bookcase.
Founded the Memphis Group in Milan.
Drew the Carlton bookcase for the first Memphis collection.
Showed the first Memphis collection in Milan, with ceramics and furniture of loud colour.

people.name: Irving Penn
people.bio: American photographer known for clean studio fashion work, still lifes and portraits in a plain corner.

milestones.event: Made his first cover for Vogue.
Photographed the Harlequin Dress for Rochas.

people.name: John F. Kennedy
people.bio: 35th President of the United States and a Harvard man. His natural-shouldered suits and easy dress made the Ivy look a national style.

emblem.credit: Glasshouse using elements by Sodacan and Heralder

milestones.event: Graduated from Harvard College.
Took office as President; his suits and bare head set the Ivy look in the news.

people.name: Aldo van Eyck
people.bio: Dutch architect who built cities from small rooms and thresholds. He was a core member of Team 10 and left the CIAM doctrine.

milestones.event: Took part in the Team 10 meeting at Doorn.
Completed the Municipal Orphanage in Amsterdam.

people.name: André Bazin
people.bio: French film critic. He co-founded Cahiers du cinéma. He argued for the long take and for realism, and he trained the critics who made the New Wave.

milestones.event: Co-founded Cahiers du cinéma.

people.name: Corita Kent
people.bio: American nun, teacher and artist who made screen prints of words and bright colour.

milestones.event: Started to teach art at Immaculate Heart College.
Became chair of the college art department.

people.name: Giancarlo De Carlo
people.bio: Italian architect and town planner of Urbino. He designed for the social and local context of a place, and he was a member of Team 10.

milestones.event: Showed a housing project for Matera at CIAM that set the rules of Le Corbusier aside for local context.

people.name: Armin Hofmann
people.bio: Swiss graphic designer and teacher at the Basel School of Design.

milestones.event: Published Graphic Design Manual.

people.name: Constant Nieuwenhuys
people.bio: Dutch painter and later maker of models for a city of the future. He was a founder of CoBrA and an early member of the Situationist International.

milestones.event: Co-founded CoBrA in Paris.
Took part in the founding of the Situationist International.

people.name: Éric Rohmer
people.bio: French critic and director. He edited Cahiers du cinéma in the late 1950s and then made talky films about moral choices.

milestones.event: Released My Night at Maud's.

people.name: Georges de Beauregard
people.bio: French film producer. He backed Breathless by Jean-Luc Godard and other films of the New Wave.

milestones.event: Produced Breathless.

people.name: Saul Bass
people.bio: American graphic designer of film titles and posters in cut-paper shapes.

milestones.event: Designed the titles of The Man with the Golden Arm.
Designed the titles of Vertigo.
Designed the title sequence of North by Northwest, an early film title with text that moves on the screen.
Designed the Bell System logo.

people.name: Timothy Leary
people.bio: American psychologist and writer who linked psychedelic culture with personal computers and became the main voice of the cyberdelic movement.

milestones.event: Used the phrase "turn on, tune in, drop out" at a press conference in New York.
Helped to create the album Cyberpunk by Billy Idol.

people.name: Andrew Grima
people.bio: Anglo-Italian jewellery designer in London. He made heavy jewels of textured gold with rough and uncut stones.

milestones.event: Showed textured gold jewels with uncut stones from his London house.

people.name: Karel Appel
people.bio: Dutch painter of thick, wild colour and childlike figures. He was a founder of CoBrA.

milestones.event: Co-founded CoBrA in Paris.
Showed in the CoBrA exhibition at the Stedelijk Museum in Amsterdam.

people.name: Christian Dotremont
people.bio: Belgian poet and painter of words. He wrote the manifesto of CoBrA and ran its journal.

milestones.event: Wrote the CoBrA manifesto La cause était entendue.

people.name: Pierre Cardin
people.bio: Italian-born French couturier. His 1960s collections of geometric tunics, tubes and helmets gave space-age dress its shapes.

milestones.event: Showed a space-age collection of geometric tunics, tubes and helmet hats.

people.name: Richard Hamilton
nationality: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
people.bio: English painter of the Independent Group who made one of the first works of Pop Art from mass-market images.

milestones.event: Made the collage Just what is it that makes today's homes so different, so appealing? for This Is Tomorrow.

people.name: Rudi Gernreich
people.bio: Austrian-born American designer. He made light, unlined clothes that follow the body, and he showed a bra without bone, pad or seam in 1964.

milestones.event: Showed the No Bra, a soft, sheer bra without bone or lining, made with a maker of foundation garments.

people.name: André Courrèges
people.bio: French couturier. His 1964 Space Age collection set the short white A-line dress, the flat trouser and the low boot as the look of the space age.

milestones.event: Opened his own couture house in Paris, after years in the atelier of Balenciaga.
Showed the Space Age collection: white A-line mini dresses, flat trousers and low boots.

people.name: Bob Maloubier
people.bio: French naval commando and diving pioneer. With Claude Riffaud he drew the diving watch that Blancpain made as the Fifty Fathoms.

milestones.event: Drew the specification for a diver's watch with Claude Riffaud; Blancpain made it as the Fifty Fathoms.

people.name: Joseph Weizenbaum
people.bio: German-American computer scientist who wrote ELIZA, the first program that held a typed conversation with a person.

milestones.event: Published ELIZA, a program that answered typed text like a therapist.

people.name: Peter Smithson
nationality: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
people.bio: English architect who, with Alison Smithson, started the New Brutalism.

milestones.event: Completed Hunstanton School, the first New Brutalist building.
Completed Robin Hood Gardens in London.

people.name: Richard Avedon
people.bio: American photographer who made fashion pictures full of motion and portraits against a plain white ground.

milestones.event: Took Dovima with Elephants in Paris.

people.name: Roy Lichtenstein
people.bio: American Pop artist who painted comic panels with Ben-Day dots.

milestones.event: Painted Look Mickey.
Painted Whaam!.

people.name: Shadrach Woods
people.bio: American architect who worked in Paris with Candilis. He was a core member of Team 10 and wrote on the street and the web as city forms.

milestones.event: Won the competition for the Toulouse-Le Mirail new town with Candilis and Josic.
Won the competition for the Free University in Berlin with Candilis and Josic.

people.name: Kazuo Shiraga
people.bio: Japanese painter who painted with his feet on large canvases and in mud. He was a leading member of Gutai.

milestones.event: Showed the mud piece Challenging Mud at the first Gutai exhibition.

people.name: Lee Iacocca
people.bio: American car executive. He led the Mustang project at Ford, a short, low, cheap car with a long list of options.

milestones.event: Joined Ford as an engineer.
Launched the Mustang at the New York World's Fair.

people.name: Peter Voulkos
people.bio: American ceramic artist who started a ceramics programme at the Otis Art Institute in Los Angeles in 1954. He threw large forms, cut and stacked them, and made clay a medium of abstract art.

milestones.event: Started the ceramics department of the Otis Art Institute in Los Angeles.
Moved to the University of California at Berkeley.

people.name: Robert Drew
people.bio: American documentary maker who led the first direct cinema films with a handheld camera and synchronised sound.

milestones.event: Founded Drew Associates.
Released the film Primary about the Wisconsin primary.

people.name: Alexander Plunket Greene
people.bio: British businessman and partner of Mary Quant. He bought Markham House in 1955 for the Bazaar boutique.

milestones.event: Bought Markham House on the King's Road.

people.name: Robert Rauschenberg
people.bio: American artist. He joined the Leo Castelli Gallery in 1958 and had his first solo show at Betty Parsons in 1951.

milestones.event: Joined the Leo Castelli Gallery.
Won the grand prize for painting at the Venice Biennale.

people.name: Robert Venturi
people.bio: American architect who argued for complexity and contradiction against the purity of Modernism.

photo.credit: todd sheridan from New York, United States

milestones.event: Completed the Vanna Venturi House in Philadelphia.
Published Complexity and Contradiction in Architecture.
Published Learning from Las Vegas with Denise Scott Brown and Steven Izenour.

people.name: Noboru Kawazoe
people.bio: Japanese architecture critic and editor, a founding member of the Metabolists. He led the theme committee of the 1960 World Design Conference with Kikutake and Kurokawa.

milestones.event: Led the theme committee for the 1960 World Design Conference in Tokyo, from which the Metabolist group came.

people.name: Paul Bocuse
people.bio: French chef of Collonges-au-Mont-d'Or near Lyon. He made the Auberge du Pont de Collonges a three-star restaurant, cooked from the market and made the chef a public figure. He started the Bocuse d'Or in 1987.

milestones.event: The Auberge du Pont de Collonges won its third Michelin star.
Created the black truffle soup for a dinner at the Élysée Palace.

people.name: Verner Panton
people.bio: Danish furniture and lighting designer of bright, curved and one-piece plastic objects.

milestones.event: Drew the Panton chair, a cantilever seat in one shell.
Saw the Panton chair go into series production in moulded plastic.

people.name: Vivian Maier
people.bio: American street photographer whose work was found after her death.

milestones.event: Her negatives were bought at an auction in Chicago.

people.name: Thea Porter
people.bio: British designer, born in Jerusalem. Her long printed dresses and caftans of Middle Eastern cloth made her a maker of hippie and bohemian dress in London.

milestones.event: Sold caftans and long dresses of Middle Eastern cloth from her Soho shop in London.

people.name: Warren Chalk
people.bio: British architect and a member of Archigram. He drew living capsules and space-age city parts.

milestones.event: Took part in the Living City show at the ICA in London.

people.name: Adrian Frutiger
people.bio: Swiss type designer whose Frutiger typeface, the humanist sans of airports and system interfaces, gave Frutiger Aero its name.

milestones.event: Released the Univers typeface.
Released the Frutiger typeface.

people.name: Agnès Varda
people.bio: Belgian-born French film director whose first film came before the New Wave.

milestones.event: Released La Pointe Courte.
Released Cléo from 5 to 7.

people.name: Alison Smithson
people.bio: English architect who, with Peter Smithson, started the New Brutalism.

milestones.event: Completed Hunstanton School with Peter Smithson.
Completed Robin Hood Gardens in London.

people.name: Andy Warhol
people.bio: American artist who used silkscreen and commercial images in Pop Art.

milestones.event: Showed Campbell's Soup Cans in Los Angeles.
Started to make silkscreen paintings and prints.
Opened the Factory studio in New York.

people.name: Christian Millau
people.bio: French food critic and writer. With Henri Gault he wrote the Gault Millau guide, which gave the new light kitchen of the 1970s a name and a list of rules.

milestones.event: Started Le Nouveau Guide with Henri Gault.
Published with Gault the ten characteristics of nouvelle cuisine.

people.name: Donald Judd
people.bio: American artist who turned a cast-iron factory building in SoHo into a home and studio and kept its open floors and large windows.

milestones.event: Bought 101 Spring Street, a five-storey cast-iron building in SoHo, New York.
Started to move his work and home to Marfa, Texas.

people.name: Fumihiko Maki
people.bio: Japanese architect who joined the Metabolists and then worked on the idea of group form. He wrote on how single buildings add up to a city.

milestones.event: Took part in the Metabolism manifesto at the World Design Conference in Tokyo.
Published Investigations in Collective Form.

people.name: Garry Winogrand
people.bio: American street photographer of New York in the 1960s.

milestones.event: Showed in the New Documents exhibition at MoMA.

people.name: Helen Frankenthaler
people.bio: American painter who stained thin paint into raw canvas and so began Colour Field painting.

photo.credit: Series: Photographs Related to the George W. Bush Administration, 1/20/2001 - 1/20/2009 Collection: Records of the White House Photo Office (George W. Bush Administration), 1/20/2001 - 1/20/2009

milestones.event: Showed the painting Mountains and Sea.

people.name: Jacques Rivette
people.bio: French critic and director. He led the group of young critics that took Cahiers du cinéma from Rohmer in 1963. His films are long and loose.

milestones.event: Released Paris Belongs to Us.
Took over the editor's chair of Cahiers du cinéma.

people.name: Kiyonori Kikutake
people.bio: Japanese architect who drew floating and raised cities. He was a founder of the Metabolists.

milestones.event: Completed his own house, Sky House, in Tokyo.
Proposed Marine City, a floating city on the sea, in the Metabolism manifesto.
Completed the Aquapolis floating platform for the Okinawa Expo.

people.name: Nelson Pereira dos Santos
people.bio: Brazilian director. His film Barren Lives showed the dry north-east with neorealist means, and many see it as a first film of Cinema Novo.

milestones.event: Released Barren Lives.

people.name: Nicolas Hayek
people.bio: Swiss businessman who took control of the Swiss watch industry group and put the Swatch at the centre of its recovery.

milestones.event: Took over the Swatch group.

people.name: Otto Piene
people.bio: German artist of light, smoke and fire. He founded Zero with Heinz Mack.

milestones.event: Co-founded Zero in Düsseldorf with Heinz Mack.

people.name: Pierre Troisgros
people.bio: French chef of Roanne. With his brother Jean he ran the Frères Troisgros restaurant and made the salmon with sorrel sauce, a sauce that the cook did not thicken with flour. Some critics call him a father of nouvelle cuisine.

milestones.event: The Frères Troisgros restaurant in Roanne won its second Michelin star.
The restaurant won its third Michelin star.

people.name: Frank Gehry
people.bio: Canadian-American architect of sculptural forms clad in metal.

photo.credit: City of Toronto / Jose San Juan

milestones.event: Rebuilt his own house in Santa Monica with chain-link and corrugated metal.
Completed the Guggenheim Museum Bilbao.

people.name: Grace Kelly
people.bio: American actress and Princess of Monaco. A photograph of her with a structured Hermès bag in 1956 made the bag known by her name.

milestones.event: Held a Hermès handbag in front of her body in a magazine photograph; the maker renamed the bag the Kelly.

people.name: Henri Gault
people.bio: French food critic. With Christian Millau he started the restaurant guide Le Nouveau Guide in 1969. He used the phrase nouvelle cuisine for the new light cooking of the chefs of his time.

milestones.event: Started Le Nouveau Guide with Christian Millau.
Published with Millau the ten characteristics of nouvelle cuisine.

people.name: Sergio Leone
people.bio: Italian director who defined the spaghetti western with extreme close-ups and wide frames.

milestones.event: Released A Fistful of Dollars.
Released The Good, the Bad and the Ugly.
Released Once Upon a Time in the West.

people.name: Claude Chabrol
people.bio: French critic and director. He was the first of the Cahiers critics to make a feature, and he later made cold thrillers about the middle class.

milestones.event: Released Le Beau Serge.

people.name: Günther Uecker
people.bio: German artist who drove rows of nails into canvas and objects. He joined Zero in 1961.

milestones.event: Joined Heinz Mack and Otto Piene in Zero.

people.name: Ikko Tanaka
people.bio: Japanese graphic designer who joined Japanese traditional forms with Bauhaus geometry in posters and brand identity.

milestones.event: Opened his own design studio in Aoyama in Tokyo.
Published the book Japan Style for an exhibition at the Victoria and Albert Museum.

people.name: Irving Blum
people.bio: American dealer of the Ferus Gallery. In 1962 he bought all 32 Campbell's Soup Cans paintings from Warhol.

milestones.event: Bought the 32 Campbell's Soup Cans paintings for 1,000 dollars.

people.name: Jasper Johns
people.bio: American artist. He joined the Leo Castelli Gallery in 1958.

milestones.event: Joined the Leo Castelli Gallery.

people.name: Jean-Luc Godard
people.bio: French-Swiss film director whose jump cuts broke the rules of film editing.

milestones.event: Released Breathless.
Released Pierrot le Fou.

people.name: Kenneth Frampton
people.bio: British architect and historian who set out the principles of Critical Regionalism in an influential essay.

milestones.event: Published the essay Towards a Critical Regionalism: Six Points for an Architecture of Resistance.

people.name: Mary Quant
people.bio: British designer. Her boutique on the King's Road sold the miniskirt and the short shift to young London, and she made the street the source of the fashion.

milestones.event: Opened the boutique Bazaar on the King's Road, London.
Showed the Wet collection of PVC raincoats.
Received the OBE for services to fashion.

people.name: Robert Arneson
people.bio: American sculptor and teacher at the University of California, Davis. His glazed stoneware toilets, typewriters and self-portraits set the style of funk ceramics.

milestones.event: Began to teach ceramics at the University of California, Davis.
Made the glazed stoneware Typewriter.

people.name: Ron Herron
people.bio: British architect and a member of Archigram. He drew the Walking City, a city that moves on legs.

milestones.event: Drew the Walking City, a set of giant machine-cities that walk.

people.name: Steve McQueen
people.bio: American film actor and racing driver. He wore a square Heuer chronograph in the racing film Le Mans, and the model took his name in the market.

milestones.event: Wore a square Heuer Monaco chronograph in the film Le Mans.

people.name: Bernd Becher
people.bio: German photographer who, with Hilla Becher, made typologies of industrial buildings.

milestones.event: Showed in the New Topographics exhibition with Hilla Becher.
Began to teach photography at the Düsseldorf Academy.

people.name: Denise Scott Brown
people.bio: Zambian-born American architect and planner who studied the commercial strip as architecture.

milestones.event: Published Learning from Las Vegas with Robert Venturi and Steven Izenour.

people.name: Gérald Genta
people.bio: Swiss watch designer. He drew the Royal Oak in 1972 and the Nautilus in 1976, the first steel sports watches with an integrated bracelet that cost as much as gold.

milestones.event: Drew the Royal Oak for Audemars Piguet, a steel watch with an octagonal bezel and eight screws.
Drew the Nautilus for Patek Philippe.

people.name: Guy Debord
people.bio: French writer and film maker. He was the main thinker of the Situationist International.

milestones.event: Co-founded the Situationist International.
Published The Society of the Spectacle.

people.name: Heinz Mack
people.bio: German artist of light and movement. He founded Zero in Düsseldorf with Otto Piene.

milestones.event: Co-founded Zero in Düsseldorf with Otto Piene.

people.name: Alexander Kluge
people.bio: German film maker, writer and lawyer. He signed the Oberhausen Manifesto and made Abschied von gestern, a first feature of the New German Cinema.

milestones.event: Signed the Oberhausen Manifesto.
Released Abschied von gestern.

people.name: Atsuko Tanaka
people.bio: Japanese artist of Gutai. She made a dress of coloured light bulbs and then pictures of linked circles.

milestones.event: Showed the Electric Dress at the Gutai exhibition.

people.name: Dieter Rams
people.bio: German industrial designer of Braun products and the ten principles of good design.

milestones.event: Designed the SK 4 radio-phonograph with Hans Gugelot.
Designed the 606 universal shelving system on a grid of rails.
Became head of design at Braun.
Gave the talk that listed his principles of good design.

people.name: Edgar Reitz
people.bio: German film maker. He signed the Oberhausen Manifesto, and later he made the long serial film Heimat.

milestones.event: Signed the Oberhausen Manifesto.
Released Mahlzeiten.

people.name: Eero Aarnio
people.bio: Finnish designer of the Ball chair and other fibreglass furniture in round forms.

milestones.event: Designed the Ball chair in fibreglass.

people.name: François Truffaut
people.bio: French critic and film director who attacked the old French cinema and then replaced it.

milestones.event: Published A Certain Tendency of the French Cinema.
Released The 400 Blows.

people.name: Richard Estes
people.bio: American painter known for exact city views with glass and street reflections made from photographs.

milestones.event: Held a one-man show at the Allan Stone Gallery in New York.

people.name: Michel Guérard
people.bio: French chef and pastry chef. He cooked at Asnières and at Eugénie-les-Bains, and made cuisine minceur for the guests of a spa. His restaurant Les Prés d'Eugénie held three Michelin stars from 1977.

milestones.event: Opened the restaurant Le Pot-au-Feu in Asnières-sur-Seine.
Moved to Eugénie-les-Bains and began his slimming cuisine for the spa guests.
Published La Grande Cuisine minceur; Time put him on its cover in February.
Les Prés d'Eugénie won its third Michelin star.

people.name: Richard Rogers
people.bio: British-Italian architect who put the services of a building on its outside.

milestones.event: Completed the Centre Pompidou in Paris with Renzo Piano.
Completed the Lloyd's building in London.

people.name: Giorgio Armani
people.bio: Italian designer. His soft, unstructured jackets in plain wool set the line of the working suit for both sexes in the 1980s.

milestones.event: Founded his fashion house in Milan with Sergio Galeotti.
Dressed the lead of the film American Gigolo in soft, unstructured jackets.

people.name: Hilla Becher
people.bio: German photographer who, with Bernd Becher, made typologies of industrial buildings.

milestones.event: Showed in the New Topographics exhibition with Bernd Becher.
Won the Golden Lion for sculpture at the Venice Biennale with Bernd Becher.

people.name: Kisho Kurokawa
people.bio: Japanese architect and writer who drew the city as a body that grows. He built the Nakagin Capsule Tower.

milestones.event: Co-wrote the Metabolism manifesto for the World Design Conference in Tokyo.
Completed the Nakagin Capsule Tower in Tokyo.

people.name: Michael Graves
people.bio: American architect of colourful Postmodern buildings and household objects.

milestones.event: Completed the Portland Building in Oregon.
Designed the 9093 kettle with a bird whistle for Alessi.

people.name: Paco Rabanne
people.bio: Spanish-born French designer. He built dresses from plastic discs and metal rings, and so made metal and plastic a material of couture.

milestones.event: Showed 12 Unwearable Dresses in Contemporary Materials, made of plastic discs and metal links.

people.name: Bodo Mans
people.bio: German ceramic designer who drew vases for the West German potteries of the 1960s and 1970s. His heavy forms carry the thick, running glazes of fat lava ware.

milestones.event: Designed vases for the Bay Keramik pottery in the mid 1960s, at the start of the fat lava years.

people.name: Dennis Crompton
people.bio: British architect and a member of Archigram. He kept the archive of the group and drew the Computer City.

milestones.event: Drew the Computer City, a city made of data and pods.

people.name: Geoffrey Lee
people.bio: British type designer who drew the Impact typeface. Meme makers later chose it for the captions of the image macro.

milestones.event: Drew Impact for the Stephenson Blake foundry.

people.name: J. Borges
people.bio: Brazilian woodcut artist and cordel poet from Bezerros in Pernambuco. He made covers for cordel chapbooks and he is known beyond Brazil.

milestones.event: The state of Pernambuco named him a Living Heritage master (Patrimônio Vivo). Some sources give 1999.

people.name: Mario Buatta
people.bio: American decorator called the Prince of Chintz, whose layered English country rooms are the source of the grandmillennial look.

people.name: Norman Foster
people.bio: English architect of High-tech buildings that show their structure and services.

milestones.event: Completed the HSBC Main Building in Hong Kong.
Won the Pritzker Architecture Prize.

people.name: Octavio Getino
people.bio: Argentine film maker and writer, born in Spain. He co-founded Grupo Cine Liberación with Solanas and co-wrote Toward a Third Cinema.

milestones.event: Co-directed The Hour of the Furnaces.
Co-wrote Toward a Third Cinema.

people.name: Fernando Solanas
people.bio: Argentine director and politician. With Octavio Getino he made The Hour of the Furnaces and wrote the text that named Third Cinema.

milestones.event: Co-directed The Hour of the Furnaces.
Co-wrote Toward a Third Cinema.

people.name: Frank Stella
people.bio: American painter whose flat black pinstripe canvases made the picture an object and not a window.

milestones.event: Showed four black pinstripe paintings in the Sixteen Americans exhibition at MoMA.

people.name: Peter Cook
people.bio: British architect and teacher who led Archigram. He drew cities as machines that plug in and change.

milestones.event: Published the first issue of the Archigram magazine with his colleagues.
Drew Plug-in City, a frame that carries replaceable units.
Received the RIBA Royal Gold Medal with the other members of Archigram.

people.name: Victor Moscoso
people.bio: Spanish-American artist of psychedelic posters with vibrating colour.

milestones.event: Made posters for the Family Dog and the Matrix in San Francisco.

people.name: David Greene
people.bio: British architect and a member of Archigram. He drew the Living Pod and wrote poems with his drawings.

milestones.event: Drew the Living Pod, a small shell for one household.

people.name: Michael Webb
people.bio: British architect and a member of Archigram. He drew the Cushicle, a worn inflatable room.

milestones.event: Showed the Cushicle, an inflatable shell that a person carries.

people.name: Renzo Piano
people.bio: Italian architect who designed the Centre Pompidou with Richard Rogers.

photo.credit: Cirone-Musi (Festival della Scienza, Genova)Color and edits by the uploader.

milestones.event: Completed the Centre Pompidou in Paris.
Completed the Potsdamer Platz tower in Berlin, which has a terracotta facade.
Won the Pritzker Architecture Prize.

people.name: Ridley Scott
people.bio: English film director whose science fiction films showed a used, hardware-heavy future with bulky screens and switches.

milestones.event: Released the film Alien.
Released the film Blade Runner.

people.name: Robert Adams
people.bio: American photographer of the suburban American West.

milestones.event: Published The New West.
Showed in the New Topographics exhibition.

people.name: Wes Wilson
people.bio: American artist who made the psychedelic concert poster with melting letters.

milestones.event: Made the first of his Fillmore posters for Bill Graham.

people.name: Andrea Branzi
people.bio: Italian architect and designer who founded Archizoom in Florence. He drew No-Stop City, a city as one endless room.

milestones.event: Conceived the Superonda sofa for Poltronova.
Took part in the founding of Global Tools in Florence.

people.name: Issey Miyake
people.bio: Japanese designer. He pressed polyester jersey into permanent pleats after the garment was cut, and so made clothes that are light and stretch.

milestones.event: Launched the Pleats Please line of heat-set pleated polyester.

people.name: Joel Meyerowitz
people.bio: American photographer who moved street photography into colour.

milestones.event: Published Cape Light.

people.name: Marcello Gandini
people.bio: Italian car designer. At Bertone he drew the low, flat wedge with a sharp crease that set the line of the supercar for 20 years.

milestones.event: Drew the Carabo show car for Bertone.
Drew the Stratos Zero show car, a wedge that was 84 cm high.
Showed the Countach prototype.

people.name: Terry de Havilland
people.bio: English shoemaker from a London shoe family. He made the bright platforms and wedges that glam rock musicians wore in the 1970s.

milestones.event: Made new three-tiered wedge shoes in snakeskin colours, from a pair that he found in his father's attic.
Became the rock and roll cobbler of the decade; his clients included David Bowie and Led Zeppelin.

people.name: Yvon Chouinard
people.bio: American climber and maker. He made climbing gear in California, and in 1973 he began to sell outdoor clothes. His firm helped to make polar fleece.

milestones.event: Began to sell outdoor clothes under the name Patagonia.
Worked with Malden Mills on a napped polyester pile that became polar fleece.

people.name: Francis Ford Coppola
people.bio: American director and a leading figure of New Hollywood who made personal films inside the studio system.

milestones.event: Released The Godfather.
Released The Conversation.
Released Apocalypse Now.

people.name: Glauber Rocha
people.bio: Brazilian director and critic. He led Cinema Novo, and he wrote the Aesthetics of Hunger, a short text on a film of poverty and violence.

milestones.event: Released Black God, White Devil.
Wrote the essay Aesthetics of Hunger.

people.name: Richard Serra
people.bio: American sculptor. Castelli found him in 1967 and offered three years of monthly payments.

milestones.event: Castelli offered him a guarantee of monthly payments.

people.name: Ruggero Deodato
people.bio: Italian director whose film Cannibal Holocaust used a found-footage plot long before the style had a name.

milestones.event: Released Cannibal Holocaust, a film built from recovered camera footage.

people.name: William Eggleston
people.bio: American photographer who made colour photography accepted as art.

milestones.event: Showed William Eggleston's Guide at MoMA.

people.name: Dario Argento
people.bio: Italian director who made the giallo famous with stylish murder films.

milestones.event: Released The Bird with the Crystal Plumage.
Released Deep Red.
Released Suspiria.

people.name: Paolo Deganello
people.bio: Italian architect and designer who co-founded Archizoom. He then made furniture for Cassina.

milestones.event: Co-founded Archizoom in Florence.
Designed the AEO armchair for Cassina.

people.name: Adolfo Natalini
people.bio: Italian architect who founded Superstudio in Florence. He wrote the texts of the group and drew the Continuous Monument.

milestones.event: Founded Superstudio in Florence with Cristiano Toraldo di Francia.
Presented the Continuous Monument with Superstudio.

people.name: Cristiano Toraldo di Francia
people.bio: Italian architect who founded Superstudio in Florence. He worked on the films and the images of the group.

milestones.event: Founded Superstudio in Florence with Adolfo Natalini.
Showed the work of Superstudio at the MoMA show Italy: The New Domestic Landscape.

people.name: Gunpei Yokoi
people.bio: Japanese engineer at Nintendo who designed the Game Boy around a cheap four-shade monochrome screen.

milestones.event: Led the design of the Game Boy and its four-shade screen.

people.name: Vivienne Westwood
people.bio: British designer. With Malcolm McLaren she made the torn, pinned, slogan-printed and bondage clothes that dressed the London punk scene.

milestones.event: Opened a shop at 430 King's Road, London, with Malcolm McLaren.
Renamed the shop SEX and sold rubber, leather and bondage clothes.

people.name: Calvin Klein
people.bio: American designer who founded a fashion house in 1968. In the 1980s his name on the waistband made plain underwear a branded and advertised product.

milestones.event: Launched the company that later took his name.
Put his name on the waistband of a plain brief and sold it as fashion.

people.name: Gerardo Vallejo
people.bio: Argentine film director, a founder of Grupo Cine Liberación with Solanas and Getino.

milestones.event: Founded Grupo Cine Liberación with Fernando Solanas and Octavio Getino.

people.name: Jeremiah Tower
people.bio: American chef. He was the chef of Chez Panisse from 1972 to 1978 and gave the daily menu its sharp, ripe and formal style. In 1984 he opened Stars in San Francisco.

milestones.event: Joined Chez Panisse as a cook and later as its chef.
Opened the restaurant Stars in San Francisco.

people.name: Rei Kawakubo
people.bio: Japanese designer. She founded Comme des Garçons and made black, loose, torn and lopsided clothes that questioned the shape of the body.

milestones.event: Founded the Comme des Garçons label in Tokyo.
Showed her first collection in Paris, in black, loose and torn clothes.
Showed Body Meets Dress, Dress Meets Body, with padded lumps on the body.

people.name: Jean-Pierre Gorin
people.bio: French film maker and teacher. He worked with Godard in the Dziga Vertov Group, and with him he made Tout va bien.

milestones.event: Co-directed Wind from the East in the Dziga Vertov Group.
Co-directed Tout va bien with Godard.

people.name: Jil Sander
people.bio: German designer. Her plain, fine and precisely cut clothes in neutral colours set the line of 1990s minimalism.

milestones.event: Opened her first boutique in Hamburg.

people.name: Ken Thompson
people.bio: American computer scientist who wrote the first Unix with Dennis Ritchie and gave the command line its plain text form.

milestones.event: Wrote the first version of Unix at Bell Labs.

people.name: Yohji Yamamoto
people.bio: Japanese designer. His long, black, oversized clothes in wool and cotton set the dark, loose line of the Japanese wave in Paris.

milestones.event: Showed his first collection in Paris, in loose black clothes.

people.name: Alice Waters
people.bio: American chef, author and food activist. She opened Chez Panisse in Berkeley in 1971 and built the menu on fresh, seasonal produce from named local farms. She also began the Edible Schoolyard project in a Berkeley school. She worked with a pottery on a dinnerware line for her restaurant.

milestones.event: Opened Chez Panisse in Berkeley.
Opened the Chez Panisse Café upstairs, with an à la carte menu.
Started the Chez Panisse Foundation and the Edible Schoolyard.
Worked with Heath Ceramics and Christina Kim on the Chez Panisse dinnerware collection.

people.name: Charles Burnett
people.bio: American director. He studied at UCLA and made Killer of Sheep, a quiet film about a family in Watts, as a student project.

milestones.event: Released Killer of Sheep.

people.name: Dapper Dan
people.bio: American tailor of Harlem, New York. In the 1980s he printed luxury logos on leather and made jackets, bags and car seats for his clients.

milestones.event: Opened his boutique on 125th Street, Harlem.
By the mid-1980s printed luxury logos on leather with a silk-screen press.

people.name: Massimo Osti
people.bio: Italian designer of Bologna. He took sport and military cloth into dress, dyed whole garments and tried new fabrics for C.P. Company and Stone Island.

milestones.event: Launched Stone Island with a jacket of heavy rubberised cloth of the type used for truck covers.

people.name: Lewis Baltz
people.bio: American photographer of industrial parks and new tract houses.

milestones.event: Showed in the New Topographics exhibition.

people.name: Patrick Le Quément
people.bio: French designer. He led the design of Renault from 1987 and made small cars with soft, round forms and bright interiors.

milestones.event: Became director of design at Renault.
Showed the Twingo, a one-box city car with a round body.

people.name: Ward Christensen
people.bio: American engineer who built the first bulletin board system, CBBS, with Randy Suess. It made the dial-up boards where ANSI art grew.

milestones.event: Started CBBS in Chicago with Randy Suess, the first public bulletin board system.

people.name: Haile Gerima
people.bio: Ethiopian-born director and teacher. He studied at UCLA and made political films on the Black experience, such as Bush Mama.

milestones.event: Released Bush Mama.

people.name: John Woo
people.bio: Hong Kong director who made gunfights that move like dance, with slow motion and wide frames.

milestones.event: Released A Better Tomorrow.
Released The Killer.
Released Hard Boiled.

people.name: Malcolm McLaren
people.bio: British impresario and shop owner. He ran the King's Road shop with Vivienne Westwood and managed the Sex Pistols, who wore its clothes.

milestones.event: Ran the SEX shop at 430 King's Road, London.
Became the manager of the Sex Pistols, and dressed the band in the shop's clothes.

people.name: Mark Perry
people.bio: English writer and musician who started the punk fanzine Sniffin' Glue.

photo.credit: The original uploader was Wwwhatsup at English Wikipedia.

milestones.event: Started Sniffin' Glue while he worked as a bank clerk.
Stopped the zine and formed the band Alternative TV.

people.name: Michel Bras
people.bio: French chef of Laguiole in the Aubrac, who built his menu from the wild and garden plants of the plateau and made the plate a small landscape.

milestones.event: Took over the kitchen of the family restaurant in Laguiole and began to cook from the plants of the plateau.
Made the first gargouillou, a dish of dozens of young vegetables, herbs and flowers.
Moved the restaurant to a new building on the Suquet plateau above Laguiole.

people.name: Axel Vervoordt
people.bio: Belgian art dealer and interior designer of rooms in raw, quiet materials.

people.name: Hajime Sorayama
people.bio: Japanese illustrator known for airbrushed chrome robots with exact reflections and bright colour.

milestones.event: Published the book Sexy Robot.

people.name: Jamie Reid
people.bio: British artist who made the ransom-note graphics of the Sex Pistols.

milestones.event: Made the cover of God Save the Queen.
Made the cover of Never Mind the Bollocks.

people.name: Søren Kragh-Jacobsen
people.bio: Danish director. He joined Dogme 95 after its start, and his film Mifune was the third Dogme film.

milestones.event: Released Mifune, Dogme film no. 3.

people.name: Stephen Shore
people.bio: American photographer of colour road trips across the United States.

photo.credit: Drpaluga (talk). Original uploader was Drpaluga at en.wikipedia

milestones.event: Published Uncommon Places.

people.name: Donna Karan
people.bio: American designer. Her 1985 Seven Easy Pieces gave the working woman a small wardrobe of bodysuit, skirt, jacket and trouser.

milestones.event: Showed Seven Easy Pieces, a system of work clothes for women.

people.name: Ed Logg
people.bio: American game designer at Atari who made arcade games for vector and raster screens.

milestones.event: Co-designed Asteroids, a vector-display arcade game.

people.name: Leonard Koren
people.bio: American writer and designer who explained the Japanese idea of wabi-sabi to Western artists and designers.

milestones.event: Published the book Wabi-Sabi for Artists, Designers, Poets and Philosophers.

people.name: Philippe Garrel
people.bio: French director who started very young. He worked with the Zanzibar group, which Sylvina Boissonnas paid for, and he made silent, black-and-white films.

milestones.event: Worked with the Zanzibar group on his first films.

people.name: Scott Fahlman
people.bio: American computer scientist who proposed :-) and :-( on a Carnegie Mellon message board in 1982.

milestones.event: Proposed :-) and :-( as marks for jokes and serious posts on a Carnegie Mellon message board.

people.name: Steve Wilhite
people.bio: American computer scientist who led the CompuServe team that made the GIF image format.

milestones.event: Led the team at CompuServe that released the GIF format.

people.name: William Gibson
people.bio: American-Canadian novelist whose stories of neon cities and networked hackers set the look and mood of cyberpunk.

milestones.event: Published the short story Burning Chrome, which used the word cyberspace.
Published the novel Neuromancer.

people.name: John Pawson
people.bio: British architect who reduces a room to light, proportion and one material, with all storage hidden.

milestones.event: Completed the Calvin Klein flagship store on Madison Avenue, New York.
Published the book Minimum.

people.name: Nobu Matsuhisa
people.bio: Japanese chef who worked in Peru and Argentina before Los Angeles. He cooked Japanese fish with Peruvian chilli and citrus and opened Matsuhisa in 1987 and Nobu in New York in 1994.

milestones.event: Opened the restaurant Matsuhisa in Los Angeles.
Opened the first Nobu in New York with Robert De Niro and partners.

people.name: Philippe Starck
people.bio: French designer. His first sanitary ware range for Duravit in 1994 treated a washbasin and a WC as designed objects, not as plain fittings.

milestones.event: Launched his first sanitary ware collection for Duravit.

people.name: Tom Truscott
people.bio: American computer scientist. As a graduate student at Duke University he planned Usenet with Jim Ellis, a news network between Unix computers.

milestones.event: Planned Usenet with Jim Ellis at Duke University.

people.name: Wolfgang Puck
people.bio: Austrian-American chef trained in France. He opened Spago in Los Angeles in 1982 and Chinois on Main in Santa Monica in 1983, where he put Chinese flavours on a French and Californian plate.

milestones.event: Opened Spago on the Sunset Strip in Los Angeles.
Opened Chinois on Main in Santa Monica.

people.name: Ken Kutaragi
people.bio: Japanese engineer at Sony who led the design of the PlayStation and its polygon hardware.

milestones.event: Led the launch of the PlayStation in Japan.

people.name: Zaha Hadid
people.bio: Iraqi-British architect of fractured and then fluid forms, the first woman to win the Pritzker Prize.

milestones.event: Showed her work in the Deconstructivist Architecture show at MoMA.
Completed the Vitra Fire Station in Weil am Rhein.
Won the Pritzker Architecture Prize.

people.name: Dave Theurer
people.bio: American game designer at Atari who made colour vector arcade games with deep perspective.

milestones.event: Designed Tempest, a colour vector game seen down a tube in perspective.

people.name: Michele De Lucchi
people.bio: Italian architect and designer, a founding member of the Memphis Group.

milestones.event: Joined the Memphis Group as a founding member.
Designed the Tolomeo lamp with Giancarlo Fassina.

people.name: Jean Paul Gaultier
people.bio: French designer who used the corset as a motif of his work and took the boned bodice and the cone bra out of the underwear drawer and on to the runway.

milestones.event: Introduced the corset with a cone bra for women.
Made the cone-bra costumes for the Blond Ambition tour of Madonna.

people.name: Julie Dash
people.bio: American director. She studied at UCLA, and her Daughters of the Dust was the first feature by a Black woman to get a US cinema release.

milestones.event: Released Daughters of the Dust.

people.name: Shigeru Miyamoto
people.bio: Japanese game designer at Nintendo who set the look of side-scrolling and top-down worlds on 8-bit hardware.

milestones.event: Directed Super Mario Bros. on an 8×8 tile grid.
Directed Super Mario 64, a free 3D camera world.

people.name: Brunello Cucinelli
people.bio: Italian designer and maker. He built a house on cashmere in soft colours and fine hand finish, made in Solomeo, Umbria, with no visible logo.

milestones.event: Began his firm with a small line of cashmere jumpers in colour.
Founded his firm with a small range of coloured cashmere jumpers.

people.name: Elmar Mock
people.bio: Swiss engineer. With Jacques Müller he built the first plastic watch of few parts, which became the Swatch.

milestones.event: Launched the Swatch watch with Jacques Müller and Ernst Thomke.

people.name: Nan Goldin
people.bio: American photographer of her own circle at night, lit by direct flash.

milestones.event: Published The Ballad of Sexual Dependency.

people.name: J Mays
people.bio: American car designer. He drew the Concept One show car for Volkswagen, and from 1997 he led design at Ford, where he revived old forms.

milestones.event: Showed the Concept One at the Detroit show.
Became vice president of design at Ford.

people.name: Shawn Stussy
people.bio: American surfboard shaper. He printed his hand-written name on T-shirts and shorts, and so began one of the first streetwear labels.

milestones.event: Began to sell T-shirts and shorts with his signature mark, from Laguna Beach, California.

people.name: Susan Kare
people.bio: American graphic designer who drew the first bitmap icons and screen fonts for the Macintosh, so that pixel graphics became a standard visual language.

milestones.event: Joined Apple and began work on the Macintosh interface elements.
Released the original Macintosh with her icons and the Chicago and Geneva typefaces.
Saw the Museum of Modern Art acquire her Macintosh icon sketchbooks.

people.name: Tim O'Reilly
people.bio: Irish-American publisher who helped name Web 2.0 at a conference in 2004 and set out its ideas in an essay in 2005.

milestones.event: Held the first Web 2.0 Conference with John Battelle; the term spread to site design.

people.name: Alexander Brodsky
people.bio: Russian architect and artist who drew etchings of strange cities with Ilya Utkin. He became a key figure of Soviet paper architecture.

milestones.event: Graduated from the Moscow Architecture Institute.
Built Palazzo Nudo, a house-shaped skeleton, in Pittsburgh.

people.name: Andreas Gursky
people.bio: German photographer who made large, cool, detailed colour pictures after study with Bernd Becher.

milestones.event: Finished his study at the Düsseldorf Academy under Bernd Becher.
Made the photograph Rhein II.
Had a solo show at the Museum of Modern Art.

people.name: Béla Tarr
people.bio: Hungarian director and a founding figure of slow cinema who made films of long takes and little plot.

milestones.event: Released Sátántangó, a film of very long takes.
Released The Turin Horse.

people.name: David Carson
people.bio: American graphic designer of layered, broken magazine type.

milestones.event: Became art director of Ray Gun magazine.
Published The End of Print.

people.name: Hervé This
people.bio: French physical chemist who studies the changes of food in the kitchen and who named the science of molecular and physical gastronomy with Nicholas Kurti.

milestones.event: Founded the workshop on molecular and physical gastronomy with Nicholas Kurti in Erice, Sicily.
Published Molecular Gastronomy: Exploring the Science of Flavor in English.

people.name: Ilya Utkin
people.bio: Russian architect who worked with Alexander Brodsky on etchings of distorted cities. The pair became known in the West as paper architects.

people.name: Lisa Frank
people.bio: American designer who founded a stationery company known for rainbow colours, bright animals and sticker sheets. Kidcore takes much from her 1980s and 1990s look.

milestones.event: Founded Lisa Frank Inc. in Tucson, Arizona.

people.name: Steve Jobs
people.bio: American co-founder of Apple who led the company when it launched the glossy Aqua interface of Mac OS X.

photo.credit: MetalGearLiquid, based on File:Steve_Jobs_Headshot_2010-CROP.jpg made by Matt Yohe

milestones.event: Introduced the Aqua interface at the Macworld Expo in San Francisco.

people.name: Tim Berners-Lee
people.bio: English computer scientist who made the World Wide Web; its first pages of raw, unstyled HTML are the model of the brutalist web.

milestones.event: Wrote the proposal for the World Wide Web at CERN.
Put the first website online at CERN.

people.name: David Bohnett
people.bio: American entrepreneur who founded Beverly Hills Internet, which became GeoCities, the free host of personal home pages.

milestones.event: The company Beverly Hills Internet took the name GeoCities.

people.name: Helmut Lang
people.bio: Austrian designer. His slim, plain and exact clothes in black, white and grey set a clean, urban line in the 1990s.

milestones.event: Founded his own label in Vienna.

people.name: Ian Anderson
people.bio: British graphic designer who founded The Designers Republic.

milestones.event: Founded The Designers Republic in Sheffield.
Designed the graphics of the game Wipeout.

people.name: Jim Ellis
people.bio: American computer scientist. With Tom Truscott at Duke University he planned Usenet, a network of discussion groups that started in 1980.

milestones.event: Planned Usenet with Tom Truscott at Duke University.

people.name: Lars von Trier
people.bio: Danish film director who wrote the Dogme 95 manifesto with Thomas Vinterberg.

milestones.event: Signed the Dogme 95 manifesto in Copenhagen.
Released The Idiots, Dogme #2.

people.name: Naoto Fukasawa
people.bio: Japanese industrial designer of quiet household products, and co-author of the Super Normal idea.

milestones.event: Showed the Super Normal exhibition in Tokyo with Jasper Morrison.

people.name: Roy Yamaguchi
people.bio: Japanese-American chef who trained in French kitchens. In 1988 he opened Roy's in Honolulu, and in 1991 he was one of the chefs who named Hawaii regional cuisine.

milestones.event: Opened the first Roy's restaurant in Honolulu.
Joined the chefs who gave Hawaii regional cuisine its name.

people.name: Yasushi Wakabayashi
people.bio: Japanese net user whom sources credit with an early upright emoticon, (^_^), posted on the ASCII NET bulletin board in 1986.

milestones.event: Posted the face (^_^) on the ASCII NET board, an early example of the Japanese upright kaomoji style.

people.name: Kristian Levring
people.bio: Danish director. He joined Dogme 95 after its start, and his film The King Is Alive was the fourth Dogme film.

milestones.event: Released The King Is Alive, Dogme film no. 4.

people.name: Nathalie Du Pasquier
people.bio: French artist who drew the patterns of the Memphis Group.

milestones.event: Joined the Memphis Group as a founding member.

people.name: Neville Brody
people.bio: British graphic designer and art director of The Face magazine.
