milestones.event: Became art director of The Face.
Published The Graphic Language of Neville Brody.

people.name: Yuri Avvakumov
people.bio: Russian architect, artist and curator who gave the name paper architecture to the Soviet scene. He organised its shows from 1984.

milestones.event: Brought the term paper architecture into Russian use.
Founded the Agitarch studio in Moscow.

people.name: Chris Stamper
people.bio: British programmer who co-founded Ultimate Play the Game and wrote its isometric engine.

milestones.event: Co-made Knight Lore, whose room engine set the isometric look on home computers.

people.name: Jasper Morrison
people.bio: British designer of plain, useful furniture and household objects, who named the Super Normal idea with Naoto Fukasawa.

milestones.event: Designed the Plywood chair for a Swiss furniture firm.
Showed the Super Normal exhibition in Tokyo with Naoto Fukasawa.

people.name: Nathan Myhrvold
people.bio: American physicist and former technology chief of Microsoft, who led the team of The Cooking Lab that wrote the six-volume book Modernist Cuisine.

milestones.event: Published Modernist Cuisine: The Art and Science of Cooking with Chris Young and Maxime Bilet.

people.name: Rand Miller
people.bio: American game designer who co-founded Cyan and co-made Myst from pre-rendered stills.

milestones.event: Co-made Myst with his brother Robyn.

people.name: Emma Bridgewater
people.bio: British potter and businesswoman. In 1985 she started a pottery in Stoke-on-Trent that makes sponge-decorated earthenware, and brought spongeware back into common use.

milestones.event: Started her pottery with sponge-decorated mugs and jugs.

people.name: Silvia Venturini Fendi
people.bio: Italian designer of accessories, a third-generation member of the Fendi family. She designed the Baguette in 1997, a small beaded bag worn under the arm.

milestones.event: Designed the Baguette, a short-strap bag that the house sold in hundreds of surfaces.

people.name: Hillman Curtis
people.bio: American designer and film maker who showed how Flash could make motion graphics for the web, and who wrote a book about it.

milestones.event: Published Flash Web Design, a guide to design in Flash.

people.name: Patrik Schumacher
people.bio: German architect and theorist who named Parametricism and wrote its manifesto while he led the office of Zaha Hadid.

milestones.event: Launched a manifesto for Parametricism at the Venice Biennale of Architecture.

people.name: Tim Stamper
people.bio: British game developer who co-founded Ultimate Play the Game and later Rare.

milestones.event: Co-made Knight Lore with its isometric room engine.

people.name: Ferran Adrià
people.bio: Catalan chef of elBulli on the Costa Brava, who made the foam, the sphere and the deconstructed dish into the language of a new kitchen.

milestones.event: Became head chef of elBulli in Roses.
Served the first siphon foams at elBulli.
Made spherification a dish at elBulli, with sodium alginate and a calcium bath.
Closed the restaurant elBulli and turned it into a foundation.

people.name: India Mahdavi
people.bio: Iranian-born French architect and designer of rooms in saturated colour.

milestones.event: Redesigned The Gallery at Sketch in London in pink.

people.name: Monky (Pedro Tolomeo Rojas Meza)
people.bio: Peruvian poster artist of Lima. He is a leading maker of chicha posters. He painted them by hand and later screen printed them.

milestones.event: Made his first posters, with stencils and spray paint.
Began to screen print posters with Juan Tenicela.

people.name: Claus Meyer
people.bio: Danish food entrepreneur who co-founded Noma and wrote the Manifesto for the New Nordic Kitchen in 2004.

milestones.event: Co-founded Noma with René Redzepi.
Called the Nordic Cuisine Symposium, where twelve chefs signed the manifesto.

people.name: Donna Tartt
people.bio: American novelist. Her novel The Secret History tells of a small circle of classics students, and it is the main text behind dark academia.

milestones.event: Published The Secret History.

people.name: Eiji Aonuma
people.bio: Japanese game director at Nintendo who directed a cel-shaded 3D world.

milestones.event: Directed The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker.

people.name: Michael Jordan
people.bio: American basketball player. His signed shoe of 1985 made the sneaker a badge of taste and a collector item.

milestones.event: His first signature shoe, the Air Jordan 1, went on sale in black and red.

people.name: Michel Gondry
people.bio: French director who made inventive music videos for Björk, the Chemical Brothers and others.

milestones.event: Made the video Human Behaviour for Björk.
Made the video Star Guitar for the Chemical Brothers.

people.name: Juergen Teller
people.bio: German photographer of raw, flash-lit fashion pictures.

people.name: Naoto Ohshima
people.bio: Japanese artist at Sega who designed characters and worlds for fast 16-bit parallax games.

milestones.event: Designed the hero and art of Sonic the Hedgehog.

people.name: Stefan Sonnenfeld
people.bio: American colourist who graded blockbusters in teal and orange.

milestones.event: Graded Transformers.

people.name: Yves Camdeborde
people.bio: French chef trained at the Ritz, La Tour d'Argent and the Hôtel de Crillon. In 1992 he bought La Régalade in Paris, cooked there at a low fixed price, and gave the bistro style a name that the press called bistronomie.

milestones.event: Bought the restaurant La Régalade in the 14th arrondissement of Paris.
Opened Le Comptoir du Relais in the Saint-Germain quarter.

people.name: Kazuko Shibuya
people.bio: Japanese pixel artist at Square who drew sprites and maps for 8-bit and 16-bit role-playing games.

milestones.event: Drew the pixel sprites of Final Fantasy.
Drew pixel art for Final Fantasy VI.

people.name: Michael Bay
people.bio: American film director whose action films made the teal and orange grade common.

milestones.event: Released Transformers.

people.name: Shinji Mikami
people.bio: Japanese game director at Capcom who used pre-rendered rooms and fixed cameras for suspense.

milestones.event: Directed Resident Evil with pre-rendered rooms.

people.name: Frédérick Raynal
people.bio: French game designer who put polygon figures over fixed, drawn camera views.

milestones.event: Made Alone in the Dark with fixed camera angles over drawn rooms.

people.name: Heston Blumenthal
people.bio: English chef of The Fat Duck in Bray, who used the lessons of food science, low-temperature cooking and play with memory to build long tasting menus.

milestones.event: Opened The Fat Duck in Bray, Berkshire.
Published The Big Fat Duck Cookbook.

people.name: John Maeda
people.bio: American designer and educator who argued that good design reduces a product to its essential parts.

milestones.event: Published the book The Laws of Simplicity.
Became the president of the Rhode Island School of Design.

people.name: Michael Green
people.bio: Canadian architect and author who argued for tall buildings of engineered wood and made mass timber known.

milestones.event: Gave a TED talk titled Why we should build wooden skyscrapers.

people.name: Robyn Miller
people.bio: American artist and composer who rendered the worlds of Myst in 3D software.

milestones.event: Rendered the island views of Myst.

people.name: Gastón Acurio
people.bio: Peruvian chef of Lima, who took ceviche and the native produce of Peru into fine dining and led the rise of Peruvian cuisine in the world.

milestones.event: Opened Astrid y Gastón in Lima with Astrid Gutsche.
Founded Mistura, the yearly food fair of Lima, to show Peruvian produce and cooks.

people.name: Jony Ive
people.bio: British designer who led design at Apple, from the translucent iMac to the flat interface of iOS 7.

milestones.event: Released the iMac G3 in translucent Bondi Blue.
Released the first iPhone.
Released iOS 7, a flat interface, as head of Human Interface design.
Led the design team that released the Apple Watch.
Left Apple and founded LoveFrom.

people.name: Franz von Holzhausen
people.bio: American car designer. He led the design of the Model S, a saloon with a smooth body and one large screen in place of a dashboard.

milestones.event: Joined Tesla as chief designer.
The Model S went on sale.

people.name: Jerry Yang
people.bio: Co-founder of Yahoo!. He and David Filo began a link directory in 1994 that grew into the model of the web portal.

milestones.event: Started the Yahoo! link directory with David Filo.

people.name: Justin Sewell
people.bio: A founder of Despair, Inc., the company that sold the Demotivators line of black-framed posters from 1998.

milestones.event: Despair, Inc. began to sell Demotivators, posters that invert the office motivational poster.

people.name: Scott Forstall
people.bio: American software engineer who led iOS at Apple in its skeuomorphic years.

milestones.event: Released the first iPhone OS as head of the software team.
Left Apple after the iOS 6 Maps launch.

people.name: Thomas Vinterberg
people.bio: Danish film director who co-wrote the Dogme 95 manifesto.

milestones.event: Signed the Dogme 95 manifesto.
Released Festen, Dogme #1.

people.name: Wes Anderson
people.bio: American director known for centred, symmetrical frames, flat camera moves and a limited colour palette.

milestones.event: Released The Royal Tenenbaums.
Released The Grand Budapest Hotel.

people.name: James Atkinson
people.bio: Software developer who started phpBB, a free and open-source forum program, in 2000.

milestones.event: Started phpBB, a free forum program.

people.name: Tim Sweeney
people.bio: American programmer who founded Epic Games and leads Unreal Engine.

milestones.event: Made Unreal Engine 4, with physically based materials, open to all for a subscription.

people.name: Tom Anderson
people.bio: American co-founder of Myspace. His profile was the first friend of each new member.

milestones.event: Co-founded Myspace.

people.name: Andoni Luis Aduriz
people.bio: Basque chef of Mugaritz near San Sebastián, who joined wild plants, odd texture and a play on the senses in one tasting menu.

milestones.event: Opened Mugaritz in Errenteria, in the hills near San Sebastián.
Published Mugaritz: A Natural Science of Cooking with Phaidon.

people.name: Olia Lialina
people.bio: Russian net artist. Her work My Boyfriend Came Back from the War used frames and plain HTML to tell a story in the browser window.

milestones.event: Published My Boyfriend Came Back from the War, a story told in nested browser frames.

people.name: Samwise Didier
people.bio: American art director at Blizzard who set its chunky, hand-painted fantasy look.

milestones.event: Art director of World of Warcraft.

people.name: Sara Blakely
people.bio: American businesswoman. She founded Spanx in Atlanta, and her footless control-top tights started the modern line of shapewear.

milestones.event: Founded Spanx in Atlanta and sold footless control-top tights.

people.name: Sean Baker
people.bio: American director who made a feature film for cinema with phone cameras.

milestones.event: Released Tangerine, shot on three iPhone 5S phones.

people.name: Yusuke Naora
people.bio: Japanese art director at Square who led the pre-rendered city and room art of Final Fantasy VII.

milestones.event: Art director of Final Fantasy VII.

people.name: Shigetaka Kurita
people.bio: Japanese designer who drew the first widely used emoji set, of 176 pictures on a 12 by 12 pixel grid, for the NTT Docomo i-mode phone.

milestones.event: NTT Docomo released his set of 176 emoji, drawn in 1998 on a 12 by 12 pixel grid, on its i-mode service.

people.name: Harmony Korine
people.bio: American filmmaker who shot on VHS and made a Dogme 95 film.

milestones.event: Released Julien Donkey-Boy, a Dogme 95 film.
Released Trash Humpers, shot on VHS.

people.name: Matías Duarte
people.bio: Chilean designer who led the creation of Material Design at Google.

milestones.event: Presented Material Design at Google I/O.

people.name: Phoebe Philo
people.bio: British designer. As creative director of Céline from 2008 she made plain, calm clothes in fine cloth that others took as the model of quiet luxury.

milestones.event: Became creative director of Céline and made plain, fine clothes with no visible logo.

people.name: Grant Achatz
people.bio: American chef of Alinea in Chicago, who turned the methods of the modernist kitchen into a tasting menu with edible balloons, hot and cold soups and a play of scent.

milestones.event: Opened Alinea in Chicago.
Published the book Alinea with Nick Kokonas.

people.name: Kikiyama
people.bio: Japanese game maker who made the free game Yume Nikki in 2004. Its dream rooms and strange places became a source of the dream image look.

milestones.event: Released Yume Nikki, a game about a girl who explores dream worlds.

people.name: Cliff Bleszinski
people.bio: American game designer at Epic who led a gritty, desaturated HD shooter.

milestones.event: Lead designer of Gears of War.

people.name: Kavinsky
people.bio: French producer whose retro synth music for the film Drive helped to make synthwave known to a wide audience.

photo.credit: Delrem at English Wikipedia cropped by MRCLD

milestones.event: Heard his song Nightcall in the opening credits of the film Drive.
Released the debut album OutRun.

people.name: Daniel Humm
people.bio: Swiss-born chef of Eleven Madison Park in New York, who changed the menu of a three-star restaurant to plant-based food in 2021, and put some animal products back in 2025.

milestones.event: Reopened Eleven Madison Park with a menu of plant-based food only.
Published Eleven Madison Park: The Plant-Based Cookbook.

people.name: Jack Dorsey
people.bio: American co-founder of Twitter, the site whose post card gave the tweet screenshot meme its frame.

milestones.event: Co-founded Twitter and sent the first public post.

people.name: Andrew Bujalski
people.bio: American director often called the godfather of mumblecore for his small, talk-based films.

milestones.event: Shot Funny Ha Ha, his first feature.

people.name: René Redzepi
people.bio: Danish chef of Noma in Copenhagen, who made foraging, fermentation and the Nordic season the frame of a tasting menu.

milestones.event: Opened Noma in Copenhagen with Claus Meyer.
Noma was first named the best restaurant of the World's 50 Best list.
Published The Noma Guide to Fermentation with David Zilber.

people.name: Virgilio Martínez
people.bio: Peruvian chef of Central in Lima, who organises the menu by altitude and uses tubers, grains and plants from the sea to the high Andes.

milestones.event: Opened Central in Lima.

people.name: Nguyễn Đăng Chế
people.bio: Vietnamese craftsman of Dong Ho village. He is one of the few masters of the Dong Ho woodblock painting who still work, and he set up the Dong Ho Painting Center.

milestones.event: Set up the Dong Ho Painting Center to keep the craft alive.

people.name: Tomoya Asano
people.bio: Japanese producer at Square Enix who started the HD-2D look.

milestones.event: Produced Octopath Traveler, the first HD-2D game.

people.name: Markus Persson
people.bio: Swedish programmer who made Minecraft and founded Mojang.

milestones.event: Released the first version of Minecraft.

people.name: Mitsuharu Tsumura
people.bio: Peruvian chef of Japanese family, known as Micha, who leads Maido in Lima and set the form of Nikkei cuisine at the top of the table.

milestones.event: Opened Maido, a Nikkei restaurant, in Lima.

people.name: Zach Barth
people.bio: American game developer who made Infiniminer, an early block-mining game.

milestones.event: Released Infiniminer, a world of mineable cubes.

people.name: Albert Shum
people.bio: Designer who led the Metro design language of Windows Phone, with its grid of live tiles.

milestones.event: Released the tile grid of Windows Phone 7 as its design lead.

people.name: Jennifer Allen
people.bio: The forum user who proposed the name autonomous sensory meridian response (ASMR) in 2010.

milestones.event: Proposed the name autonomous sensory meridian response for the effect.

people.name: Lewis Hilsenteger
people.bio: Canadian-American video maker who runs the Unbox Therapy channel, a model of the plain, top-down unboxing video.

milestones.event: Started the Unbox Therapy channel on YouTube.

people.name: Casey Neistat
people.bio: American filmmaker and YouTuber who made the daily vlog a cinematic form.

milestones.event: Started his daily vlog on YouTube.
Founded Beme, a video app.

people.name: Greg Lutze
people.bio: Co-creator of VSCO, the photo app that made preset codes such as A6 a common way to edit.

milestones.event: Co-created VSCO Cam with Joel Flory.

people.name: Jamie Beck
people.bio: American photographer who made the first cinemagraphs with the motion designer Kevin Burg in 2011.

milestones.event: Released the first cinemagraphs with Kevin Burg during New York Fashion Week.

people.name: Joel Flory
people.bio: Co-creator of VSCO, the photo app whose film-stock presets set a matte look for phone photos.

milestones.event: Co-created VSCO Cam with Greg Lutze, a photo app with film-style presets.

people.name: Kevin Burg
people.bio: American motion designer who made cinemagraphs with the photographer Jamie Beck from 2011.

milestones.event: Built the looping motion of the first cinemagraphs with Jamie Beck.

people.name: Lil Internet
people.bio: American DJ who used the word seapunk in a joke tweet in 2011. The word named the ocean theme that spread online.

milestones.event: Posted the word seapunk in a tweet about a leather jacket with barnacles.

people.name: Nathan Williams
people.bio: Co-founder of Kinfolk magazine, whose calm, natural-light still lifes of tables and objects shaped the flat lay look.

milestones.event: Co-founded Kinfolk, a magazine of slow-living photo spreads.

people.name: Sahil Lavingia
people.bio: American entrepreneur who founded Gumroad, whose 2021 redesign made Neo-Brutalism popular.

milestones.event: Founded Gumroad.
Released the Neo-Brutalist redesign of Gumroad.

people.name: Takeshi Idezawa
people.bio: Japanese executive of the company behind the LINE messenger, which launched in 2011 and made sticker packs a core part of chat.

milestones.event: Led the company that launched the LINE messenger, later known for its sticker packs.

people.name: Daniel Lopatin
people.bio: American musician whose slowed loops prepared the sound of Vaporwave.

milestones.event: Released Chuck Person's Eccojams Vol. 1.

people.name: Eric Migicovsky
people.bio: Canadian engineer who founded Pebble. His crowd-funded smartwatch of 2012 raised more money than any project before it on Kickstarter.

milestones.event: Raised funds for the Pebble smartwatch on Kickstarter.

people.name: A. G. Cook
people.bio: British producer and founder of the label PC Music. Spotify editors call him a godfather of hyperpop.

milestones.event: Founded PC Music, whose cover art mixes pastel gloss, 3D and web clutter.

people.name: Alan Dye
people.bio: American designer who led the Human Interface team at Apple.

milestones.event: Worked on the user interface of iOS 7.
Presented the interface of visionOS.

people.name: Alexis Ohanian
people.bio: American co-founder of Reddit, a main home of deep-fried and surreal meme communities.

milestones.event: Co-founded Reddit.

people.name: Emily Segal
people.bio: American writer and trend forecaster. She co-founded the trend group K-Hole, whose 2013 report Youth Mode brought the word normcore into use.

milestones.event: Took part in the K-Hole report Youth Mode, which named normcore as a choice to blend in.

people.name: Greta Gerwig
people.bio: American director and writer. Her film Barbie and its pink sets and costumes set off the Barbiecore trend in fashion and online images.

milestones.event: Released the film Barbie, which carried the pink look to a mass audience.

people.name: Justin Kan
people.bio: American founder of Justin.tv, the live video site from which the game stream platform Twitch grew.

milestones.event: Launched Twitch as a game-only branch of Justin.tv.

people.name: Kevin Systrom
people.bio: Co-founder of Instagram, the app that added the swipe carousel post in 2017.

milestones.event: Co-launched Instagram, with filters and square photos.
Led Instagram as the feed moved to a ranked order and profiles became curated grids.
Led Instagram as it added posts with up to 10 photos in one swipeable carousel.

people.name: Mike Grabarek
people.bio: Co-founder of the first Health Goth group on Facebook. The group mixed goth mood, sport and net art images.

milestones.event: Started the Health Goth Facebook community with Jeremy Scott and Chris Cantino.

people.name: Rosa Menkman
people.bio: Dutch artist and theorist of glitch art, author of the Glitch Studies Manifesto and The Glitch Moment(um).

milestones.event: Published the Glitch Studies Manifesto, a text on the creative use of errors.
Published The Glitch Moment(um) with the Institute of Network Cultures.

people.name: Steve Huffman
people.bio: American programmer who co-founded Reddit with Alexis Ohanian and wrote much of its first code.

milestones.event: Co-founded Reddit.

people.name: Zhang Yiming
people.bio: Founder of ByteDance, the company behind Douyin, TikTok and CapCut.

milestones.event: ByteDance merged Musical.ly into TikTok, the app that carries the Duet tool.
ByteDance launched CapCut, the editor with the velocity tool.

people.name: Alex Zhu
people.bio: Co-founder of Musical.ly, the short-video app where users mimed songs in 15-second clips.

milestones.event: Co-founded Musical.ly, an app for 15-second lip-sync videos.

people.name: Ken Wong
people.bio: Australian game artist who was lead designer of Monument Valley at ustwo.

milestones.event: Lead designer of Monument Valley.

people.name: Tony Zhou
people.bio: Video maker who made the series Every Frame a Painting with Taylor Ramos, short film essays with clean type and clips.

milestones.event: Started the series Every Frame a Painting on Vimeo and YouTube.

people.name: Alexander Mordvintsev
people.bio: Researcher at Google who wrote the code that made DeepDream, the first widely shared neural network image effect.

milestones.event: Wrote the DeepDream code and posted its first images at Google.

people.name: Antonio Guillem
people.bio: Spanish photographer whose stock photo of three people on a street became the base of the Distracted Boyfriend label meme.

milestones.event: Took the stock photo that the label meme later used.

people.name: Elliot Túpac
people.bio: Peruvian artist (born Elliot Urcuhuaranga Cárdenas) who makes chicha posters and shows them abroad.

milestones.event: Showed chicha art at the Smithsonian Folklife Festival in Washington, D.C.

people.name: Jason Citron
people.bio: American entrepreneur who co-founded Discord, a chat app for communities that began with gamers.

milestones.event: Launched Discord with Stanislav Vishnevskiy.

people.name: The Cobrasnake
people.bio: American nightlife photographer whose direct-flash party photos defined the 2000s blog era.

people.name: Tobias van Schneider
people.bio: German designer who led product design at Spotify and set trends in flat interface and brand design.

milestones.event: Worked on the duotone brand of Spotify as lead designer.

people.name: David Karp
people.bio: American entrepreneur who founded Tumblr, the blog site where reblogged photo feeds spread the soft grunge look.

milestones.event: Founded Tumblr, a microblog site built on reblogged images.

people.name: Justus Thies
people.bio: German computer scientist who co-wrote Face2Face, a real-time method that carries one face's expression onto another face in video.

milestones.event: Co-wrote Face2Face, a real-time face re-enactment method for video.

people.name: Morikura En
people.bio: A Japanese illustrator. The Kizuna AI article credits Morikura with the character design of Kizuna AI, the first channel that called itself a virtual YouTuber.

milestones.event: Drew the character design of Kizuna AI, the anime-style avatar of the first virtual YouTuber.

people.name: Vincent Van Duysen
people.bio: Belgian architect and designer of calm interiors in natural materials.

milestones.event: Became creative director of Molteni&C.

people.name: Michelle Phan
people.bio: American video maker whose make-up tutorials on YouTube set a model for talk-while-you-prepare videos.

milestones.event: Posted make-up tutorial videos on YouTube.

people.name: Xoana Herrera
people.bio: Illustrator who drew Alegria, the illustration system that started Corporate Memphis.

milestones.event: Drew the Alegria illustration system for Facebook at Buck.

people.name: Breogán Hackett
people.bio: Irish game developer who founded Haunted PS1, a community for games in the style of the first PlayStation.

milestones.event: Founded Haunted PS1.
Released the Haunted PS1 Demo Disc.

people.name: Christopher Poole
people.bio: American founder of 4chan, the imageboard where the rage comic, the image macro and the wojak face spread.

milestones.event: Founded the imageboard 4chan.
Opened 4chan on the model of the Japanese board Futaba Channel.

people.name: Tero Karras
people.bio: Researcher at NVIDIA and lead author of StyleGAN, the face generator behind the generated headshot.

milestones.event: Published StyleGAN with Samuli Laine and Timo Aila.

people.name: Alexander Plyuto
people.bio: Ukrainian designer whose Skeuomorph Mobile Banking shot started the Neumorphism trend.

milestones.event: Posted the Skeuomorph Mobile Banking shot on Dribbble.

people.name: Felix Kjellberg
people.bio: Swedish video maker whose gameplay videos with a face window and loud captions set the form of the facecam commentary.

milestones.event: Opened the YouTube channel that later became the model of gameplay with a facecam.

people.name: Michal Malewicz
people.bio: Polish designer who named Glassmorphism and Neumorphism in his articles.

milestones.event: Named the trend Neumorphism in an article.
Named the trend Glassmorphism in an article.

people.name: Olivier van Herpt
people.bio: Dutch designer who builds his own clay printers and prints vessels in earthenware and stoneware. The wall of each vase shows the layer lines of the printer.

milestones.event: Showed vases from a clay printer that he built himself.

people.name: Taylor Swift
people.bio: American singer and songwriter. Her 2020 album Folklore, with its forest and cabin images, took cottagecore to a wide audience.

emblem.credit: Original: Taylor Swift / UMG Vector: SINGmeAsadSONG

milestones.event: Released the album Folklore, which pop media linked with the cottagecore look.

people.name: Alexis Barreyat
people.bio: French developer who co-created BeReal, the app that posts a back and a front camera photo at the same time.

milestones.event: Released BeReal with Kévin Perreau.

people.name: Zach King
people.bio: American filmmaker of short magic edits on Vine and TikTok.

milestones.event: Became known for six-second magic edits on Vine.

people.name: Jane Remover
people.bio: American musician. Wikipedia calls her the face of digicore, the music scene that grew with glitchcore edits.

milestones.event: Spread digicore sound and a fast, glitch look in the scene on SoundCloud and Discord.

people.name: Jay Christensen
people.bio: American drone pilot whose one-shot FPV flight through a bowling alley made cinematic FPV widely known.

milestones.event: Flew the one-shot FPV film Right Up Our Alley in Minneapolis.

people.name: Boris Dayma
people.bio: Machine learning engineer who made DALL-E Mini, the free image model that later took the name Craiyon.

milestones.event: His DALL-E Mini model went viral and filled feeds with 3x3 smudge grids.

people.name: Kane Parsons
people.bio: American filmmaker and creator who posts as Kane Pixels. His Backrooms videos gave the empty-room look of liminal spaces a story and a wide audience.

milestones.event: Posted The Backrooms (Found Footage) on YouTube.

people.name: Kyle Edward Ball
people.bio: Canadian film maker. He directed Skinamarink in 2022 and said that he looked at the online Weirdcore and Liminalspace groups while he worked on it.

milestones.event: Directed Skinamarink, a film with a low-quality, empty-house look that readers link to weirdcore.

people.name: Maxime Heckel
people.bio: Design engineer who writes about WebGL, shaders and 3D effects in the browser.

milestones.event: Published The Study of Shaders with React Three Fiber.
Spoke at Figma Config 2025.

people.name: Robin Rombach
people.bio: Researcher and lead author of the latent diffusion paper, the base of Stable Diffusion and of the glossy image look of open text-to-image models.

milestones.event: Latent diffusion paper appeared at CVPR; its method became the base of Stable Diffusion.

people.name: Vektroid
people.bio: American musician who made Floral Shoppe, the album that set the look of Vaporwave.

milestones.event: Released Floral Shoppe as Macintosh Plus.

people.name: Emil Kowalski
people.bio: Design engineer who worked at Vercel and Linear and makes open-source interface components with detailed motion.

milestones.event: Released Sonner, a toast component for React.

people.name: Simon Willison
people.bio: British programmer and writer who promoted the word slop for unwanted AI-made content in 2024.

milestones.event: Wrote a widely shared post that made slop the common name for unwanted AI-made content.

people.name: Hailey Bieber
people.bio: American model and founder of a skin-care brand. Media link her dewy skin, slick bun and neutral dress with the clean girl look.

milestones.event: Launched the skin-care brand Rhode, with a glazed skin look as its image.

people.name: MrBeast
people.bio: American video maker whose thumbnails, with a large face, a few words and strong colour, are a model of the clickbait still.

milestones.event: Gained a large audience with stunt videos that used bold, face-led thumbnails.

people.name: Khaby Lame
people.bio: Senegalese-Italian creator of silent short videos, for a time the most-followed person on TikTok.

milestones.event: Became the most-followed person on TikTok.
